170996c614912a89: KUALA LUMPUR: Former world keirin champion Azizulhasni Awang is back racing in Shanghai after more than two decades and he has made it clear he is not there to make up the numbers.
Azizulhasni and the rest of the national squad will be racing at the Shanghai World Championships on Oct 14-18, which also marks the start of the Olympic qualifying window for Los Angeles 2028.
The 38-year-old will be competing in the men's individual sprint (Oct 17) and his specialty, the keirin (Oct 15).
Azizulhasni said his desire to be the best remains just as strong as it was at the start of his career.

"From competing at the Shanghai Asia-Pacific Championships in an outdoor velodrome in 2004 to now competing at the 2026 World Championships in an indoor velodrome, a lot has changed after 22 years," said Azizulhasni on social media today.
"But one thing remains unchanged, I am still hungry for success. My fighting spirit has never faded.
"I can't wait to give it another crack here."
Azizulhasni will be racing at the relatively new, state-of-the-art Shanghai Velodrome, which was officially opened in May 2024.
Despite his advancing years, Azizulhasni has been in the form of his life this season.
The 38-year-old became the overall keirin champion of the UCI World Cup series after winning two gold (Perth, Nilai) this season.
He also won the keirin gold at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games in August, a title which had long eluded him.
At the start of this month, he won the keirin gold and the individual sprint bronze at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.

The other national riders who have made the trip to Shanghai are Shah Firdaus Sahrom, Fadhil Zonis, Akmal Jusena, Ridwan Sahrom, Izzah Izzati Asri, Nur Alyssa Farid, Aliana Azizan and Anis Amira Rosidi.
962b560928712d71: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Egypt will hold a Joint Commission meeting in the first quarter of next year to strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade, investment and transportation.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the two countries' foreign ministers had agreed to the meeting.
"Whilst we have achieved a phenomenal increase this year, rising to 74.7 per cent of trade, but that is from a very, very low base.

"Therefore, collaboration with Egypt will give Malaysia immense opportunities to expand trade, investment, tourism and cooperation across various sectors," he said at a joint press conference with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi.
El-Sisi is in Malaysia for his first state visit to the country since assuming office in June 2014. The visit is at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
Anwar said other potential areas of bilateral cooperation included semiconductors, electrical and electronics (E&E), agriculture and pharmaceuticals.

"We have been trying to source pharmaceutical products from emerging economies and BRICS countries, and I think Egypt has the potential to be one destination that we solicit pharmaceutical products from."
Education was another important area of cooperation, with opportunities extending beyond Islamic studies to engineering, medicine, E&E, digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI), he said.

"I have told President El-Sisi that education in Egypt is not limited to Al-Azhar University, which remains important for Islamic education. Egypt has also expanded its capabilities in E&E, digital technology, AI, engineering and medicine.

"Many of our doctors received their training in Egypt. I do not want to create the impression that only Islamic studies are important. While they remain significant, educational cooperation should also encompass other fields of study," he said.
Anwar added that both countries should strengthen cooperation in defence procurement and joint training.
"Although our countries are geographically distant, our hearts are close," he said.
Anwar said his meeting with El-Sisi also covered international issues, including the unresolved situation in the Strait of Hormuz and its implications for Iran.
"We have taken a strong position against the atrocities inflicted upon the people of Palestine and Gaza, as well as the intransigence and violence perpetrated by Israel."
He said Egypt had provided substantial assistance to Malaysia in its efforts to deliver humanitarian aid to the Palestinians, although Malaysia's contribution was modest compared with Egypt's.
"You have provided tremendous help and assistance to the Palestinians. Malaysia has also contributed, albeit on a smaller scale, through you and your office personally.
"When we brought injured Palestinians from Gaza to Malaysia, we coordinated through your office and your military intelligence."
d89e51b4f811cf6f: GUA MUSANG, Oct 10 — The Federal Route FT08 along the Gua Musang-Kota Bharu Road, near Taman Rekreasi Kesedar here, has been closed to all vehicles today due to a sinkhole measuring about eight metres deep.
The incident, reported at 9.05am, affected a stretch of about nine metres between Sections 205.556 and 205.564, involving the alignment of Packages 3B and 3C of the Central Spine Road (LTU) project.
According to reports by the Gua Musang Public Works Department (JKR) and Roadcare (M) Sdn Bhd, the closure wasn implemented to ensure the safety of road users while further action is taken.
Road users are advised to use alternative routes via FT2747, namely Jalan Pulai to Bandar Baharu Gua Musang.
Meanwhile, Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo, when contacted, confirmed the incident and advised road users to comply with instructions from the authorities. — Bernama
aa5595ede15cb9b6: BUKIT MERTAJAM: An 84-year-old man was injured when a crane overturned and crashed onto the roof of an elderly care home in Permatang Tinggi today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 12.38pm.
He said the crane was believed to have lost stability while parked on uneven ground before overturning and striking the roof of the dormitory housing residents.
"The victim sustained a head injury and was taken to hospital by Health Ministry personnel before firefighters arrived," he said.
John said a total of 49 people, comprising residents and workers, were at the premises when the incident occurred.
They included 20 men, one of whom was injured, 17 women and 11 workers, including the crane driver.
Firefighters monitored the affected area to ensure safety and cordoned off the scene to control public movement and prevent unauthorised entry.
The operation was brought under control at 1.15pm and concluded at 1.45pm, involving police and Health Ministry personnel.
6184d817ae1d2a91: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi komited memastikan peruntukan dan inisiatif yang diumumkan dalam Belanjawan 2027 dilaksanakan secara berkesan, telus dan berimpak tinggi.

Katanya, setiap inisiatif yang diumumkan merupakan pelaburan strategik bagi memastikan manfaat pendidikan tinggi dapat dirasai secara langsung oleh mahasiswa, graduan, warga akademia, institusi dan masyarakat.

"KPT yakin bahawa pelaburan ini akan memperkukuh kedudukan Malaysia sebagai hab pendidikan tinggi global, sekali gus melahirkan generasi berilmu, berkemahiran, berakhlak dan berupaya memacu kemajuan negara," menurut kenyataan.
Dalam Belanjawan Persekutuan 2027 yang dibentangkan semalam, KPT menerima peruntukan sebanyak RM19.1 bilion berbanding RM18.6 bilion pada tahun 2026, meningkat RM500 juta atau kira-kira 2.6%.

Daripada jumlah tersebut, RM15.13 bilion diperuntukkan bagi perbelanjaan mengurus, manakala RM3.96 bilion bagi perbelanjaan pembangunan, merangkumi pelbagai inisiatif untuk memperkukuh prasarana, meningkatkan kualiti pendidikan, memperkasa penyelidikan dan inovasi serta menjaga kebajikan mahasiswa.

"Secara keseluruhannya, Belanjawan 2027 memperlihatkan pendekatan seimbang antara pembangunan prasarana, kebajikan mahasiswa, sokongan kepada graduan, pemerkasaan penyelidikan dan pembangunan bakat masa hadapan," katanya.

Kementerian menarik perhatian peruntukan sebanyak RM800 juta untuk menaik taraf prasarana usang di institusi pendidikan tinggi awam (IPTA), termasuk kemudahan bilik kuliah, kediaman mahasiswa dan peralatan pembelajaran.

KPT berkata usaha itu diperkukuh melalui pembangunan Residensi Mahasiswa Universiti Malaya yang bakal menyediakan kemudahan penginapan berkapasiti 10,000 mahasiswa, serta pelaburan RM750 juta oleh Kumpulan Wang Persaraan (Diperbadankan) menerusi Projek Vista Kampus di enam IPTA.

Turut disentuh peningkatan bantuan subsidi tiket penerbangan FLYSiswa kepada RM500, yang dijangka memanfaatkan lebih 60,000 mahasiswa IPTA, khususnya dalam meringankan kos perjalanan antara Semenanjung, Sabah dan Sarawak.

Pada masa sama, Program Dapur Siswa MADANI di universiti awam serta memperluas pelaksanaannya ke politeknik dan institut pendidikan guru memastikan lebih ramai pelajar mendapat akses kepada makanan pada harga berpatutan sepanjang tempoh pengajian.

Insentif potongan cukai pendapatan sehingga 10% bagi sumbangan pihak luar kepada IPTA pula dijangka menggalakkan penglibatan sektor korporat, industri, alumni dan masyarakat dalam menyokong pembangunan universiti serta kesejahteraan warga kampus.

Dalam pada itu, KPT menyambut baik langkah kerajaan memperkenalkan fleksibiliti bayaran balik pinjaman Perbadanan Tabung Pendidikan Tinggi Nasional yang dijangka memanfaatkan lebih 400,000 peminjam, antaranya penangguhan bayaran balik bagi peminjam berpendapatan bawah RM2,500 sebulan, bayaran minimum RM50 bagi mereka yang berpendapatan antara RM2,500 hingga RM3,000, serta diskaun 10% kepada peminjam tanpa tunggakan yang membuat bayaran secara konsisten.
"Insentif potongan cukai kepada majikan yang membantu melunaskan pinjaman pendidikan pekerja turut mencerminkan pendekatan lebih menyeluruh dalam meringankan komitmen kewangan graduan," katanya.

Sementara itu, KPT berkata penubuhan Dana UNIVC bernilai RM50 juta melalui kerjasama Kerajaan dan KWAP merupakan langkah strategik dalam merapatkan jurang antara penyelidikan, inovasi dan keperluan pasaran. Katanya, dana itu akan membuka lebih banyak peluang kepada penyelidik untuk menterjemahkan hasil penyelidikan serta harta intelek universiti kepada produk dan teknologi bernilai komersial.

"KPT komited memastikan setiap peruntukan dan inisiatif yang diumumkan dilaksanakan secara berkesan, telus dan berimpak tinggi, selaras dengan aspirasi Rancangan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia (RPTM) 2026–2035 untuk membangunkan ekosistem pendidikan tinggi yang inklusif, berkualiti, berdaya saing dan berteraskan kemanusiaan," katanya.
RPTM adalah rangka strategik 10 tahun bagi memperkukuhkan sistem pendidikan tinggi negara, dan sebahagian daripada gagasan besar reformasi pendidikan negara.
7b9306de8e04ad17: KUALA LUMPUR: There are concerns that hosts Malaysia may have to reduce the number of events at next year's 2027 Asean Para Games (APG) after the 2027 Budget announcement.
An allocation of RM240 million was announced on Friday for Malaysia to organise both the 2027 SEA Games and 2027 APG.
However, Paralympic Council of Malaysia president Datuk Seri Megat D Shahriman Zaharudin said the allocation was considerably lower than the RM700 million organisers had expected for the two Games.
"We were told that it was RM700 million… RM350 million to be given to the Asean Para Games, and RM350 million allocated for the SEA Games," he said.
"If we have a budget that is less to host the Games, we might have issues putting on more events."
The shortfall could force organisers to reconsider the planned 18-sport programme for the APG, with Megat saying that some sports might have to be dropped.
"When the budget is slashed, we might not be able to go beyond 18, or we might need to cut two sports.
"I do not want to upset the Asean countries, the 11 nations participating next year, because we will face a lot of pushback due to a shrinking allocation."
This could also affect preparations by participating countries, whose athletes train for specific disciplines.
Megat has appealed to the Youth and Sports Ministry to ensure the allocation for the APG is not affected.
"I hope that alongside this week of debate, we ensure that the Asean Para Games budget will not be touched and will not be reduced," he said.
Despite the hosting challenges, the 2027 Budget delivered substantial commitments for the broader sporting ecosystem, earmarking RM460 million for national sports development.
It covers high-performance initiatives including the Road to Gold Olympic programme, sports facility maintenance nationwide, as well as dedicated support systems for para-athletes and deaf sports.

The government has also set aside RM30 million in sports matching grants to encourage sports bodies to stage high-performance events, while raising the allocation for school sport activities by 50 per cent to RM27 million to benefit 10,000 schools.
ada2aa73b04e5645: AUCKLAND: New Zealand powered clear in the second half to beat Australia 50-19 on Saturday, extending their remarkable unbeaten record at Eden Park and retaining the Bledisloe Cup.
The All Blacks led 17-14 at half-time before scoring five tries in the second spell as they stretched their run of matches without defeat at the Auckland venue to 54.

The hosts put the disappointment of their recent 3-1 series loss to South Africa behind them while handing a first defeat in six Tests to Wallabies coach Les Kiss since succeeding Joe Schmidt in July.

The seven-try performance means the All Blacks retain the Bledisloe Cup – the trophy contested annually between the two nations – for a 23rd straight year regardless of the result of next week's second Test in Sydney.
The Sydney match takes on extra significance as the same two teams will contest a Rugby World Cup pool match there in a year's time.
Damian McKenzie kicked 15 points with the boot and helped spark some slick All Blacks attacks from fly-half.
However, it was his opposite, Ben Donaldson, who created both of Australia's first-half tries, tapping the ball on cleverly for fullback Tom Wright for the opener.
New Zealand responded smartly through tries to back-rowers Peter Lakai and Tupou Vaa'i, with McKenzie's eye for a gap twice playing a role.
McKenzie's penalty pushed the hosts 17-7 clear but a Donaldson break sent Wallabies captain Harry Wilson over just before the interval.
New Zealand took control after the break, with rapid-fire strikes resulting in tries to scrum-half Cam Roigard and captain Codie Taylor.
Any hopes of a late Wallabies rearguard disappeared when Leroy Carter backed up the outstanding Lakai to score.
Carter appeared to injure his leg in the process of scoring, putting him in doubt for the Sydney Test.
Carter's replacement Josh Moorby and Will Jordan both crossed late for New Zealand while Josh Nasser rounded out Australia's scoring. - AFP
1705d980b8a49d70: Nearly a third of developers who use AI daily spend four hours or more of their working day with it, according to Stack Overflow's latest survey. The survey received 30,903 responses from developers and technologists across 169 countries. Among the 10,926 daily AI users who answered the time-use question, about 80 percent reported using the tools for at least an hour a day. The research by developer Q&A site Stack Overflow also found skepticism from developers toward using AI in their roles. Only about 7 percent of developers said they trusted AI output for important work decisions, while 48 percent trusted it when they could easily verify the output. Seventy-nine percent considered source attribution important or very important when deciding whether to trust an AI-generated technical answer. Stack Overflow CEO Prashanth Chandrasekar said developers were highly skeptical as a group. "As AI agents become rapidly more autonomous, that skepticism now acts as a critical safeguard. As agents take on more work, developers need to know where an answer came from, what context informed the information that was produced or a decision that was made, and the most crucial piece – that they can actually verify its accuracy and relevance. Trust is not a given when it comes to developers; it is earned through transparency, source attribution, and rich technical context." The survey found that coding assistants or coding agents are used by 66 percent of respondents, general-purpose chat tools by 63 percent, and automated agent workflows by 26 percent. Seventeen percent of respondents said they did not use AI tools. Stack Overflow's commercial relationships with AI companies have proved contentious. In early 2024, it introduced OverflowAPI, offering paid access to its question-and-answer content and requiring participating AI providers to attribute answers to relevant posts. A couple of months later, users began to revolt against its partnership with OpenAI, which allowed the LLM builder to train AI models using 15 years of users' contributions. The Q&A site was also set to benefit from the deal by getting access to OpenAI's technology. A number of users said they'd rather remove their posts and risk their reputation scores than have their contributions train OpenAI models. The survey also found that 52 percent of respondents had learned a new coding skill or programming language this year. AI code-generation tools were among the most common learning resources, behind technical documentation. ®
271a193099e2d11b: MANDALIKA: Spain's Marc Marquez seized the lead from compatriot Jorge Martin in the MotoGP world championship following victory in a thrilling and chaotic sprint race in Indonesia on Saturday.
Ducati's reigning seven-time world champion took the chequered flag in a dramatic lap 3 sprint to go four points clear of his fellow Spaniard in the standings.
Martin, who had led the race on his Aprilia at the halfway point, finished fourth in blistering hot and dry conditions at the Mandalika International Circuit.
Japan's Ai Ogura and Italy's Fabio Di Giannantonio were second and third.
There was mayhem at the start as Spain's debutant pole-sitter Raul Fernandez and Marco Bezzecchi collided and crashed out on the first corner.
Martin took full advantage to seize the lead, with championship rival Marquez second, both having started from the second row.
With his compatriot breathing down his neck, Martin held his nerve to streak 1.5 seconds ahead at the halfway stage.
But the former world champion, having been cruising, then abruptly slowed up and surrendered the lead to Marquez, possibly because of tyre pressure issues.
That gifted the lead to Marquez, who romped home for his first win in Indonesia.
The grand prix is on Sunday.
There are just five race weekends after this, starting in Australia in a fortnight.
72f3ba094f648cde: KUALA LUMPUR: ​​​"Praise be to God, I am now officially the husband of my beloved partner, Bella."
​This was the emotional relief expressed by Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, 34, after marrying popular singer and actress Bella Astillah, 32, with a single lafaz.
Despite his experience with intense parliamentary debates, Syed Saddiq admitted that the wedding morning brought entirely new levels of nerves.
​"Earlier on, there were some nerves; I thought I was overconfident. Debating is no problem, being in Parliament is no problem.
"But earlier, I was nervous, and my hands were even shaking," he shared with wedding host and radio presenter Radin after the akad nikah.
​"Yet, praise be to God, once it was official, everything settled down. When Dr Zulkifli pronounced that we were married, that was the most important moment," he added.
​Bella—born Dayang Ara Nabellah Awang Astillah—shared her deep gratitude for the smooth ceremony, held on Level 118 of Menara Merdeka 118.
She also extended appreciation to her fans, known as BASS, for their unwavering support.
"I'm truly honoured today, grateful to God that everything proceeded smoothly," she said.
"Thank you to everyone who constantly prayed, who supported us, and who has kept us in their thoughts right up to this day. We appreciate it very much, praise be to God."
​Reflecting on their journey from working partners to life partners, Syed Saddiq thanked the public for their enduring well-wishes through past hurdles.
"Thank you for always praying for our journey. There have been ups and downs, alongside occasional hurdles and challenges," he said.
"But I believe that with everyone's blessings and prayers, praise be to God, I have been successfully united with Bella."
​The couple was married at 10.41am by former Federal Territories Mufti Datuk Seri Dr Zulkifli Mohamad Al-Bakri.
The ceremony, which was broadcast live, featured an all-white theme with Arabic and Islamic design elements, witnessed by close family and friends.

43c0a1e6917e6cbf: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning, with heavy rain and strong winds expected across all states until 6pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the warning covers the whole of Perlis, Terengganu, Negri Sembilan, Melaka, and the Federal Territories.
In Kedah, affected areas include Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Padang Terap, Sik, and Baling.
In Penang, the warning applies to Northeast (Timor Laut) and Southwest (Barat Daya) districts.
For Perak, affected areas include Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, and Hulu Perak.
In Kelantan, affected areas cover Kuala Krai and Jeli, while in Pahang, the warning involves Rompin and Jerantut.
In Selangor, the warning covers Sabak Bernam, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Petaling, and Hulu Langat, while in Sarawak, the warning covers Sri Aman (Lubok Antu).

In Sabah, affected areas include Tawau (Tawau, Semporna, Kunak, and Lahad Datu), Sandakan (Kinabatangan, Sandakan, Telupid, Labuk and Sugut, and Paitan), West Coast (Kota Belud and Ranau), and Kudat (Kota Marudu).

Thunderstorm warnings are short-term alerts issued when there are signs of thunderstorms with rain intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that are occurring or expected to last for more than an hour. The warning is valid for up to six hours.
addea1ed13e7a64f: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia dan Mesir akan menumpukan usaha untuk memperluas kerjasama perdagangan dan pelaburan, meningkatkan kesalinghubungan penerbangan serta meneroka bidang baharu ekonomi pada mesyuarat Suruhanjaya Bersama yang dijadualkan pada suku pertama tahun depan.

Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim berkata, pertemuan itu yang dipersetujui oleh menteri luar kedua-dua negara akan menyediakan platform untuk menterjemahkan hubungan dua hala yang semakin berkembang kepada peluang ekonomi yang lebih luas.

Beliau berkata, perdagangan dua hala meningkat sebanyak 74.7% pada tahun ini, namun pertumbuhan itu bermula daripada asas yang rendah, sekali gus memberikan ruang yang luas untuk pengembangan selanjutnya.

"Kita mencapai peningkatan luar biasa ini pada tahun ini, (perdagangan) melonjak kepada 74.7%, namun ia bermula daripada asas yang sangat, sangat rendah," kata perdana Menteri pada sidang media bersama Presiden Mesir Abdel Fattah El-Sisi bersempena dengan lawatan negara beliau selama dua hari ke Malaysia.

Perdana menteri berkata, Malaysia melihat potensi besar untuk memperluas kerjasama dengan Mesir dalam beberapa sektor, termasuk semikonduktor, elektrik dan elektronik (E&E), pertanian serta farmaseutikal.

Malaysia juga menyasarkan ekonomi sedang pesat membangun, termasuk negara-negara BRICS, sebagai sumber berpotensi bagi produk farmaseutikal, dengan Mesir antara negara yang mampu memenuhi keperluan tersebut.
"Mesir berpotensi menjadi destinasi untuk mendapatkan bekalan farmaseutikal," kata Anwar.
040943f1694ac8ed: IPOH: School authorities have completed administrative procedures, including discussions with the victims' families, following separate bullying and alleged teacher assault cases in Chemor and Pengkalan Hulu.

Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said investigations into both cases had been handed over to the police after the victims lodged reports.
Khairudin said the district education offices (PPD) and state Education Department had completed their administrative processes.
"This involved consensus meetings between the PPD, the schools and the victims' families to find the best win-win solution.
"The Education Ministry's 1-3-7 reporting procedure was followed to ensure harmony in schools is maintained," he said.
He urged all parties to allow the police to complete their investigations, adding that certain details only became clear after police reports were lodged.
"For example, in the Chemor case, the police report was only lodged in October, although the incident occurred in July," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after representing the Perak Menteri Besar at the state-level National Sports Day celebration at the Perak Youth and Sports Complex today.
Khairudin said he could not comment further as police investigations were ongoing.
On Oct 5, it was reported that single mother Noor Azwani Ahamad, 43, claimed her two sons had been bullied and subjected to violence involving students and a teacher at a school in Chemor.
In a separate incident in Pengkalan Hulu on Sept 23, an 11-year-old boy claimed a teacher had hit him on the head.
50ee22a391b39d02: KUALA LUMPUR: The prospect of another heritage player potentially representing Harimau Malaya has drawn attention among Malaysian football fans after 18-year-old Middlesbrough defender Cayden Cole confirmed his maternal family roots in Beranang, Selangor.
The teenage left-back addressed speculation about his ancestry in a post on his personal Instagram account (@iamcaydencole3), captioned: "for everyone asking"
Cole is the son of former Chelsea, West Ham United and England international striker Carlton Cole, while his younger brother, Cody Cole, is developing in the West Ham United academy.

The post indicated that the London-born defender could be eligible to represent England, Sierra Leone, Nigeria or Malaysia, with his Malaysian connection traced to his maternal grandmother, who was born in Beranang.
Cole, who joined Middlesbrough's Under-21 squad after developing at Hull City, has also represented Sierra Leone at Under-20 level.
His previous appearances at youth level do not necessarily rule out a future switch of international allegiance, although any change would be subject to FIFA's eligibility regulations.
However, with fans urging the FA of Malaysia (FAM) to explore the possibility, the process would require careful verification of his family records and eligibility under the relevant regulations.

Malaysian football remains under scrutiny following the eligibility controversy involving seven foreign-born players, which resulted in FIFA disciplinary action over falsified documents relating to claims of Malaysian ancestry.
The episode damaged the national body's reputation and raised questions about the verification procedures used in establishing players' eligibility.
Any assessment of Cole's potential eligibility would therefore need to be supported by authenticated civil records and the relevant checks with the authorities.
Establishing a Malaysian-born grandparent alone does not automatically settle every question concerning a player's eligibility or the procedures required to represent the national team.

There are also practical considerations beyond ancestry. For players raised and developed overseas, questions surrounding citizenship, documentation and the commitment required to represent Malaysia can complicate the process.

The experience of United States-based midfielder Wan Kuzain Wan Kamal, whose potential pathway to Harimau Malaya attracted attention ahead of the 2019 SEA Games, illustrates the challenges that can arise when eligibility and administrative requirements are not straightforward.
632981d2f0d2ee33: MEXICO CITY: A journalist was shot dead on Friday in Mexico, according to human rights NGO Article 19, the ninth to be killed in the country this year.

Hamurabi Huesca Manzano, the owner of a news website with more than 52,000 followers, was gunned down in Oaxaca state in the south of Mexico, Article 19 said, adding to a tally of journalist homicides tracked by Reporters Without Borders.
Huesca Manzano died from gunshot wounds when an armed group opened fire on him and two other men, according to the state prosecutor's report.
His website, Pinotepa Comunica, published news about politics and local issues in Santiago Pinotepa Nacional, the city where he lived.
He was also a taxi driver.
"We demand that the (prosecutor's office) treat his journalistic work as a priority in its investigation," Article 19 wrote on X.
Mexico is one of the most dangerous countries in the world to practice journalism, with more than 150 media professionals killed since 1994, according to Reporters Without Borders.
48f67435ce59322a: KUALA LUMPUR: National track cycling head coach (sprints) Harnizam Basri has yet to decide whether to field Shah Firdaus Sahrom in the men's team sprint event at the Shanghai World Championships (Oct 14-18).
Shah has not qualified for the men's individual sprint nor the men's keirin at the world meet, thus the team sprint is the only event he is eligible to compete in.
Harnizam, however, said it is too early to make a decision.
"Shah has made the trip to Shanghai but at the moment we do not know yet whether he will race in the team sprint event," said Harnizam when contacted in China today.
"He has been shortlisted for the team sprint and we are still going through a trial period.
"We will make the decision on race day."
Fadhil Zonis, Akmal Jusena or Ridwan Sahrom - Shah's younger brother - have established themselves as Malaysia's main team sprint trio over the past two seasons.
One of them, however, will have to make way for Shah if he gets the nod to race the event at the new Shanghai Velodrome.
Shah, who underwent knee surgery late last year, has yet to regain top form.

He managed a decent 9.850 seconds during the men's individual sprint qualifying at the recent Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games though this was still some way off his personal best of 9.481s from early last year. He also reached the keirin final in Japan.

6c3986e9c32847be: From Saraani Vengadesen
Malaysia talks increasingly about becoming a high-income, knowledge-based economy. We talk about artificial intelligence, digitalisation, advanced manufacturing and jobs of the future.
But there is another group of young Malaysians whose future deserves more attention: our life sciences graduates.
I often hear that Malaysia is lacking life sciences graduates.
As a biotechnology graduate, I find that statement difficult to reconcile with my own experience and with the experiences of many graduates I have encountered.

Malaysia has universities offering biotechnology, microbiology, biochemistry, molecular biology, genetics, food science and other life sciences programmes. Every year, students graduate from these courses hoping to build careers in science.

Yet many soon discover that finding a job directly related to their degree is not straightforward. So, do we really lack life sciences graduates, or do we lack life sciences jobs? There is an important difference.

Malaysia has invested in biotechnology and the bioeconomy for years. We have national policies, research institutions, universities and programmes designed to develop the sector. We continue to encourage young people to pursue science and technology.
But somewhere between graduating from university and entering the workforce, the pathway becomes unclear.

This is not because life sciences are becoming less relevant. Quite the opposite. The world is entering an era where biology is increasingly central to how we address major challenges, from food security and climate change to new medicines, sustainable materials and agricultural innovation.
The question is whether Malaysia is creating enough opportunities for the people trained to work in these fields.
For too many graduates, the options appear to be limited: remain in academia, compete for a small number of research positions, continue studying or take a job outside their field.
We often respond by saying that graduates need to become more “industry-ready.”
But perhaps we should also ask whether the industry is ready to absorb the talent our universities are producing.
A life sciences career should not mean spending an entire career at a laboratory bench or leaving the field altogether.

The modern life sciences sector needs people who understand science and can work across disciplines. There are careers in regulatory affairs, biosafety and biosecurity, science communication, intellectual property, technology transfer, clinical research, agricultural policy, food systems, environmental management, business development and science and technology governance.
These pathways exist, but they are rarely visible to students.
Malaysia also needs to look beyond producing graduates and start thinking about building a life sciences workforce.

We need better data on where life sciences graduates go after university. We need stronger university-industry partnerships, meaningful internships, industry-linked curricula and clearer pathways from research to employment.
Most importantly, we need to create and attract companies and institutions that can provide meaningful careers for this talent.
Research cannot remain trapped in laboratories and universities.
A discovery only creates wider value when it moves through the ecosystem from research to innovation, regulation, investment, commercialisation and ultimately society.
Our life sciences graduates should be part of that entire journey.
Malaysia has invested significantly in building its scientific and biotechnology capabilities. We should not allow the people trained to sustain that ecosystem to become an afterthought.
The future of work is changing rapidly. Our graduates will need interdisciplinary skills, digital literacy and the ability to work across science, technology, policy and society.
But they also need something equally important: an economy that has a place for their expertise.
If we want Malaysia to be a knowledge economy, we cannot only ask our young people to acquire the skills of the future.
We must also build the future in which those skills are needed.
Saarani Vengadesen is CEO and founder of Orbis Policy Consulting.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
08957de46db73cd2: KUALA LUMPUR: Strong enforcement and integrity among customs officers are essential to preventing cargo fraud, as legislation alone cannot stop shipments from being unlawfully diverted, a former deputy public prosecutor says.

Devanandan Subramaniam, who previously served as a commercial crime deputy public prosecutor at the Attorney-General's Chambers, said weaknesses in customs procedures could allow cargo to be discharged even when essential ownership documents are missing.

"You can have all the legislation in place, no integrity, things can still go past," he said at a forum titled "Strengthening Malaysia's Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia Regulatory Landscape".

Devanandan was asked to explain the challenges of prosecuting cargo fraud cases, including the distinction between suspicious transactions and criminal offences, the process from investigation to prosecution, and the parties who could ultimately be charged.
He was also asked to share his experience handling such cases and advise the shipping industry on compliance measures to prevent cargo fraud.
Drawing from a case he prosecuted more than 20 years ago, Devanandan recounted how cargo worth about US$2 million, originally destined for Chittagong, Bangladesh, was diverted to Port Klang.
He said the shipment originated from Belawan, Sumatra, but the charterer subsequently instructed the vessel's master to discharge the cargo in Port Klang instead.
The consignor, however, retained the original bills of lading, which served as evidence of title to the goods.
Despite this, the cargo was discharged after the clearance agent obtained the necessary approvals.

Devanandan said investigations uncovered forged documents, including K1 forms, prompting the prosecution of the company's managing director for using a forged document as genuine and the company for receiving stolen property.
However, the case was eventually thrown out after the prosecution failed to establish that the managing director knew, or had reasonable grounds to know, that the documents were forged.
He said prosecuting such cases was challenging because proving that a document was fraudulent did not necessarily establish the accused person's knowledge of the forgery.
Devanandan stressed that customs officers played a critical role in ensuring that cargo documentation was properly verified before goods were released.
"They play the most important role. As long as they ensure that everything is in order, such things will not happen," he said.
While acknowledging that cargo documentation processes had evolved towards electronic transmission since the case he handled, Devanandan said enforcement and integrity remained essential safeguards.
He added that procedural requirements would be ineffective if officers failed to ensure compliance at the point of clearance.

fd35421318223a13: LONDON: Xabi Alonso has defended Cole Palmer's commitment to England after Thomas Tuchel said the Chelsea forward had missed too many opportunities to play for the national team.
Palmer pulled out of the England squad for their recent Nations League matches against Spain, Croatia and the Czech Republic with an injury.
It was not the first time Palmer had withdrawn from international duty since Tuchel took charge of the Three Lions.

Blues boss Alonso was quick to come to the defence of Palmer, who has been a key figure for Chelsea, netting four times in seven appearances so far this season.
Pressed on whether the 24-year-old was fully engaged with England, Alonso told reporters on Friday: "He's committed, but he needs to be fully fit to play.

5f9da6e3f4e16e21: YOKOHAMA, (Japan): Double major winner Xander Schauffele moved four shots off the lead in Japan after carding two eagles and a double bogey on "a weird day" at the US PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic on Saturday.

The American had a roller-coaster front nine in sunny conditions in Yokohama, starting with a bogey before holing two birdies and an eagle on the par-5 fourth.
Schauffele followed that up with a double bogey on the next hole before sinking another eagle on the par-5 sixth, and went on to card four more birdies and another bogey to finish the round.
"It was a weird day," said Schauffele, who won Olympic gold in Tokyo in 2021.
"It was a lot of good, honestly some really bad in there as well.
"But overall, if someone told me I was going to shoot 65, I'd probably take it."
Michael Brennan, Zach Bauchou and Jacob Bridgeman lead the field heading into the final day on 13-under par.
Bridgeman is looking for his third win on the tour this year.
The trio hold a one-stroke lead over a chasing pack that includes Australia's Adam Scott.

Matsuyama, the 2021 champion in Japan, started like a freight train, rattling in four birdies and an eagle on the first seven holes.

Three-time major winner Jordan Spieth was six shots off the lead after shooting a 3-under-par 68 to finish 7-under overall.
Spieth is looking for his first win on the tour since April 2022.
Collin Morikawa, the 2023 champion in Japan, was on 4-under overall. — AFP

c85f70993e7e5ac2: OCTOBER 10 — A government that tells people to stay indoors while pollution crosses its borders owes them more than another advisory. It owes them a legal strategy that makes those responsible answer for the damage. Malaysia should begin assembling cases against haze polluters now and put a firm deadline on legislation capable of reaching them.

The factual starting point matters. In a statement reported on September 30 and reproduced by Nadma on October 1, 2026, the Department of Environment attributed Malaysia’s haze to smoke from hotspots in Kalimantan and central and southern Sumatra. Kuala Lumpur was among the places reporting unhealthy air quality. That supports investigation of a transboundary source; it does not establish the guilt of any particular company.

The next task is to identify who controlled the affected land, what they did or failed to do, and whether their conduct caused the pollution reaching Malaysia. An accusation against an entire country will never substitute for a properly constructed case against those legally responsible.

Malaysia should insist that Indonesia fulfil its international obligations. It should pursue any Malaysian corporate involvement with equal determination. A Malaysian connection must never become a reason to soften an investigation.

The Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution already supplies a legal basis for demanding action. Article 3(1) recognises responsibility for preventing activities within a state’s jurisdiction or control from harming neighbouring environments and human health. Article 4 requires cooperation and domestic implementation. Crucially, Article 4(2) requires a state from which haze originates to respond promptly to affected states’ requests for relevant information or consultations. Article 9 addresses prevention and control of fires.

Putrajaya should invoke these provisions formally, requesting concession maps, operator identities, fire-control records and enforcement outcomes. Each request should specify a proposed response date, followed by a public account of what was supplied and what remains outstanding, subject to legitimate investigative confidentiality. Diplomatic correspondence should produce evidence and corrective action.

International law also reaches beyond the treaty. In Pulp Mills on the River Uruguay in 2010, the International Court of Justice explained the duty of due diligence to prevent significant transboundary environmental damage. This is not automatic state liability whenever smoke crosses a border. The inquiry concerns whether the state took the preventive measures reasonably required of it. That distinction makes scrutiny of regulation and enforcement essential.

Malaysia should ask precise questions. Were known fire risks addressed? Were operators supervised? Were credible warnings acted upon? Where evidence establishes a breach of international obligations and resulting compensable harm, Malaysia should pursue a properly quantified claim for reparation, subject to the applicable rules on bringing that claim.

A government that tells people to stay indoors while pollution crosses its borders owes them more than another advisory. It owes them a legal strategy that makes those responsible answer for the damage. — Bernama pic

Domestic legislation must proceed alongside that effort. On September 25, 2026, Bernama reported that the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry was examining mechanisms for a specific transboundary haze law, including Singapore’s approach. That report described a proposal under examination. The public is entitled to a drafting timetable and a parliamentary deadline.

Singapore’s Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014 provides a concrete starting point. Section 4 expressly extends to overseas conduct causing or contributing to haze pollution in Singapore. Sections 5 and 6 provide for criminal and civil liability. On conviction for an offence under section 5(1), section 5(2)(a) permits a basic fine of up to S$100,000 for each day or part of a day of qualifying haze pollution. Section 5(5) imposes the applicable S$2 million aggregate ceiling. Sections 9 and 10 provide preventive-notice and information-gathering powers.

Malaysia should design its own law around demonstrable harm within Malaysia, with clearly defined offences, fair defences and effective civil remedies. Penalties should reflect the gravity and duration of the offence and remove its economic advantage. A fine that can be comfortably absorbed as an operating expense offers little deterrence.

Corporate responsibility must extend to the people and entities whose own conduct warrants it. The proposed law should address parent companies that direct or knowingly condone harmful operations, and directors whose consent, connivance or culpable neglect is proved. Liability should follow evidence of responsibility. Share ownership or a position on an organisation chart should not, by itself, establish guilt.

Article 7(1) of the Federal Constitution prohibits punishment for conduct that was not punishable when it occurred, and heavier punishment than the law then prescribed. New haze offences must respect that protection. Current conduct should be assessed under laws already applicable to it. The urgency of the crisis requires disciplined lawmaking and cases capable of surviving judicial scrutiny.

A statute will accomplish little without an enforcement plan. Singapore’s experience is instructive: in a parliamentary reply dated 13 September 2021, its government said legal notices had been issued to six Indonesian companies in connection with the 2015 haze. Two cases had been closed following information supplied; investigations into four remained open at that time. Legislation does not remove the difficulty of obtaining evidence across borders.

Malaysia should therefore establish a permanent investigative team combining environmental scientists, corporate investigators and government lawyers. Its work should connect verified fire locations with land control, operational decisions, smoke movement and harm in Malaysia. Satellite observations must be corroborated. The Department of Environment itself explains that hotspot detection can produce false indications and can be obstructed by cloud cover.

Investigators should preserve relevant records immediately and examine competing explanations, including domestic pollution. They should identify defendants against whom proceedings can realistically be brought and assets against which any judgment could lawfully be enforced. Malaysia should seek cooperation with Indonesian authorities and counsel for evidence and proceedings there. Investigative work in Indonesia should proceed through lawful arrangements that respect its sovereignty.

Compensation must become a central objective. The proposed statute should expressly allow recovery of proven medical expenses, lost earnings and other defined losses caused by the pollution. It should also provide a lawful route for recovering reasonable public expenditure on emergency response and treatment. Collective claims procedures and litigation support should make credible cases affordable for ordinary people.

The government should begin recording those losses now. Hospitals and public agencies should preserve attributable expenditure; affected businesses and individuals should retain evidence of their losses. Every claim must confront causation, competing sources and the danger of double recovery. A defensible account of damage will carry more weight than an inflated headline figure.

Commercial consequences should reinforce liability. Malaysia should legislate proportionate public-procurement exclusions for companies found responsible for serious haze offences, with notice, review and clear conditions for reinstatement. It should require relevant corporate disclosures about overseas fire risks and measures taken to control them. Public money should not reward businesses that repeatedly disregard enforceable environmental duties.

The same seriousness must apply at home. Section 29A of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 prohibits open burning, subject to the statutory framework and exclusions. Malaysia should enforce its domestic controls rigorously while pursuing transboundary sources. Credibility requires both.

ASEAN’s enforcement arrangements also need strengthening. Article 27 of the haze agreement provides for settlement of disputes through consultation or negotiation. It does not itself create a compulsory judicial route. Malaysia should propose an additional binding instrument providing independent fact-finding, compliance deadlines and arbitration accepted by participating states.

Nor should ministers promise an effortless lawsuit at the International Court of Justice. Its jurisdiction in contentious cases rests on state consent. A viable jurisdictional basis must be established. Malaysia should assess that route seriously while pursuing the evidence, domestic proceedings and negotiated remedies available to it.

The government should announce three deadlines: within 14 days, establish the investigative team and issue formal treaty requests; within 30 days, publish a legislative consultation paper and begin systematic loss documentation; within 90 days, table a bill accompanied by an enforcement budget and a plan for international evidence cooperation. These are proposed deadlines for government action, not deadlines found in the existing treaty.

The public should then receive regular progress reports on investigations and legal action, without compromising fair trials. Success must be measured by fires prevented, compliance secured and legally recoverable losses paid.

Malaysia has no obligation to make avoidable pollution politically comfortable. Where evidence supports prosecution, prosecute. Where the law permits recovery, pursue the claim. Where legal powers are missing, Parliament must supply them.
A change in the wind may clear the skyline. It cannot discharge anyone’s responsibility for the damage already done.
* The author is an associate professor with the Faculty of Law, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.

4bb1ee4fffe1e686: PARIS: Serbia will play their next home game behind closed doors and their FA has been fined 50,000 euros ($56,000) after fans engaged in racist and discriminatory behaviour in Nations League matches against Greece and Netherlands, UEFA said on Friday.

The UEFA Control, Ethics and Disciplinary Body (CEDB) also fined the Serbian FA 22,500 euros for "transmitting messages not fit for a sports event", 2,000 euros for lighting pyrotechnics and 15,000 euros for a pitch invasion during the two matches, both of which Serbia lost 2-1 last month.

Serbia were fined a further 20,000 euros for transmitting a message not fit for a sports event during that match.

Kosovo were fined 15,000 euros for displaying a message not fit for a sports event and another 20,000 euros for racist and discriminatory behaviour by fans during a 3-1 Nations League loss to Austria last month. UEFA also imposed a one-match ban on away ticket sales, suspended for two years.

Croatia were fined 20,000 euros and handed a one-match ban on away ticket sales, suspended for two years, following racist and discriminatory behaviour by supporters during a 4-1 thrashing by world champions Spain last month. - Reuters
4e67d083d48facb4: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has shared the meanings of selected words used in his 2027 Budget speech, shedding light on terms that convey ideas about governance, heritage and intergenerational responsibility.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, shared the definitions in a Facebook post today, inviting the public to learn the meanings behind the words.
Among the words he highlighted were waad, meaning a promise or pledge; lighad, meaning tomorrow or the future; and seyogia, meaning what should or ought to be done.
Other terms included beranotasi, referring to additional explanatory notes; menata, meaning to arrange or organise systematically; and inayat, referring to help or divine grace.
Pranata refers to a system or set of rules governing social life, while filasuf means philosophers.
Anwar also highlighted Ithaca, an ancient Greek island known in literature as the homeland of Odysseus. It is often associated with memories of home, history and an enduring sense of belonging.

Other words included dasawarsa, meaning a period of 10 years or a decade; khulasah, meaning a summary or the essence of an issue; and turath, referring to inherited intellectual and scholarly traditions, particularly in Islamic thought.
Anwar also highlighted the expression zaman mansang, linking it to the German term Zeitgeist, which describes the spirit, defining characteristics and demands of a particular era.

The expression carries a deeper sense of the responsibilities and obligations imposed by the times, including the need for the present generation to act responsibly towards those who come after them, a concept known as intergenerational responsibility.
2b5c4d2c609d3333: PETALING JAYA: Negeri Sembilan Umno chief Jalaluddin Alias has denied claims he intends to table a motion of no confidence against menteri besar Ismail Lasim during the coming state assembly meeting.

47a28e0a3cd67119: SHANGHAI: Daniil Medvedev fought back to beat Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff 4-6, 6-4, 6-3 in the second round of the Shanghai Masters on Saturday, the Russian's first match since being disqualified from the China Open.

The former world number one said it was an accident.

He faces either Czech qualifier Dalibor Svrcina or Tomas Martin Etcheverry of Argentina in the next round.

b6166e44438f1ff0: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Umno Negeri Sembilan Jalaluddin Alias menafikan dakwaan beliau akan mengemukakan usul undi tidak percaya terhadap Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim pada sidang DUN akan datang.

6f9094e9bbc14fd2: IPOH, Oct 10 — A man lost about RM12.47 million after his crypto assets were believed to have been stolen through unauthorised access to his digital wallet.

e1f19a014ba94a30: Microsoft has joined the Jev fan club, an accidental group of companies that share a common desire to be recognized for their own decision models. Jev, announced by TypeSafe AI three weeks ago, is a large language model (LLM) tuned to respond to certain types of questions with a limited range of responses, rated by probability. Due to its speed, relative affordability, and response constraints, it's well-suited for a variety of business applications where open-ended text of uncertain accuracy might be undesirable. One of the selling points of Jev is that decision models don't hallucinate in the way that standard LLMs do. But decision models can make errors and their popularity has already prompted researchers to explore how those errors might be magnified. Nonetheless, they have their uses. The attention lavished on Jev prompted other companies to declare that they too have decision models to offer, even though machine learning researchers have long been able to create classifier models for probability-based decisions. OpenAI said its Decisions API has entered public beta. Cloudflare chimed in with its Clef model. Strands trotted out Strands Decider 2B, "a small, open source, decision model." Liquid AI introduced d1. Perplexity launched its Decisions API. Snowflake talked up its own decision model. Then there's Surogate Rune and H2O.ai's H2O-Lightning-4B, a decision model built on Qwen3.5-4B. All told, more than 100 such models are now vying for attention. Now it's Microsoft's turn. "Decision models are quickly emerging as an important new category in AI," said Achint Srivastava, VP of software engineering in the Office of the CTO at Microsoft, in a blog post on Friday. "Unlike LLMs, which are designed to generate text or reason through complex problems, decision models are purpose-built to deliver structured outputs that software can immediately act on. And once you understand that capability – making decisions and classifying things at very low cost with high performance – all kinds of useful tasks get unlocked." Microsoft's entrant into the race is called Microsoft-Decision-1, which is offered via Microsoft Foundry and, soon, via OpenRouter. Redmond's decision model, like H2O's, is based on a Qwen model, Qwen3.5-9B in this instance. The Qwen model family is developed by Alibaba Cloud, the cloud computing arm of Chinese tech giant Alibaba. Microsoft, for reasons not disclosed, said it will soon rebase the Decision-1 on its models and those from OpenAI. The US software giant claims its model is 2.5x faster than H2O-Lightning-4B and 2.8x faster than Jev in its latency test, leads the pack in accuracy (83.5 percent) on 36 benchmarks, ranks second (behind Quyet-1.0-Large) in confidence score (92.2 percent), and is more than 20x cheaper than OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol in text classification tasks. Input tokens cost $0.042 per million tokens and output tokens are free. "Now that agentic AI is a reality, we’ve seen that cost plays a major role in how people decide to use AI," said Srivastava. "And it’s increasingly important to choose the right model for the right job." ®
ef59dc0ddfc4c134: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must strengthen maritime surveillance and enforcement to detect suspicious ship-to-ship (STS) oil transfers amid allegations that its waters are being used to facilitate the movement of sanctioned Iranian oil, an academic says.
Maritime industry and logistics expert Prof Nazery Khalid said authorities should step up patrols and use satellite technology and intelligence-sharing to identify suspicious vessel movements.

"The Coast Guard and Maritime Division should conduct patrols to keep an eye on ships behaving suspiciously," he said at a forum titled "Strengthening Malaysia's Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia Regulatory Landscape.
The forum was organised by Maritime Network, together with Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT).
Nazery said STS transfers were legitimate and highly regulated maritime operations, but must comply with national rules and international safety and environmental standards.

He said satellite monitoring could help authorities identify vessels remaining close to one another for extended periods, while specialised service providers could assist enforcement agencies in detecting suspicious activities.
"We need to ensure that ship-to-ship transfer is done in accordance with national rules, in designated areas, and ensuring that it adheres to high safety and environmental standards," he said.
Another panellist, Orkim chief executive officer Captain Cheah Sin Bi, said vessels with suspicious histories and operating practices could provide warning signs of potentially illicit transfers.
He cited vessels that had changed names repeatedly, switched registrations between countries and switched off equipment during transfers.

"The name has changed like 15 times. The registry has changed about five different countries, and then the equipment has been switched off during the transfer, so you think that something is not right," he said.
Cheah said shipping operators should conduct proper know-your-customer checks, scrutinise contractual arrangements and consult their Protection and Indemnity clubs when uncertain about a transaction.
He also urged operators to question unusually lucrative offers that deviated from prevailing market rates.
85641c1b4554690d: PETALING JAYA: Selangor coach Kim Pan Gon wants his returning international players to bring their experience and confidence to the pitch ahead of Sunday's FA Cup quarter-final second leg against Star City.

"Going through the last FIFA period, our seven international players should have gained a lot of game experience and confidence," Pan Gon said.
"Hopefully, their adaptation back into our team will give us a higher-quality game. From this match, they can contribute to help our team win."
Several Selangor players featured for their national teams during the inaugural competition in Jakarta, with midfielder Nooa Laine and defender Quentin Cheng among Malaysia's regular starters.

Faisal Halim, who was also part of Malaysia's campaign, sustained calf and tendon injuries during the tournament in Indonesia. His recovery timeline remains uncertain, leaving his availability for Selangor's return leg in question.
Pan Gon stressed that Selangor must maintain their focus despite their healthy advantage, with a place in the semi-finals at stake.
"For us, the FA Cup is very, very important," he said.

"Even though we are three goals ahead, we cannot lose our tension. We need everybody to support each other to make it perfect and go to the semi-final. We will try our best for this game, and our fans also need to come out and support us."
The South Korean also hope the team's performance and the backing of the home crowd will help build momentum for the remainder of the campaign.
"As always, when we play against any opponent in our home game, the atmosphere is very, very important to gain more confidence," he said.
"We will try our best to play our best game to attract fans to come all the time for home games. For this match, please come to support us and make it our festival."
fca5ba8e9d9f3043: PETALING JAYA: All Women’s Action Society (Awam) menggesa Ahli Parlimen meneliti Belanjawan 2027 menerusi lensa jantina apabila ia dibahaskan dalam beberapa minggu akan datang, menegaskan ia masih belum mencukupi untuk menangani isu berlarutan yang membelenggu wanita.

Presiden Awam Lai Suat Yan berkata, walaupun belanjawan kali ini membawa beberapa penambahbaikan, termasuk bantuan tambahan untuk kerja penjagaan, peruntukan cuti bersalin lebih baik serta penaiktarafan kemudahan asuhan di premis kerajaan, ia secara keseluruhannya tetap 'mengecewakan'.

Lai berkata, belanjawan tersebut gagal menangani isu-isu seperti keganasan berasaskan jantina, kadar penyertaan tenaga kerja yang rendah, dan beban kerja penjagaan tanpa gaji yang tidak seimbang secara menyeluruh.

“Banyak keperluan sekian lama wanita Malaysia masih belum dipenuhi, dan keadaan ini akan terus memberi kesan terhadap hak, keselamatan serta kesejahteraan mereka sepanjang tahun depan,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

“Golongan wanita masih jauh daripada mencapai kesaksamaan dan pariti. Oleh itu, Awam menegaskan belanjawan awam wajar dinilai melalui lensa responsif jantina bagi memastikan dana awam menangani ketidaksamarataan sedia ada, menyantuni pelbagai keperluan wanita, serta menyumbang kepada pembangunan negara yang inklusif dan mampan.”

Di bawah Belanjawan 2027 yang dibentangkan semalam, beberapa inisiatif serta manfaat bersasar untuk wanita telah diperuntukkan, antaranya cuti bersalin lebih panjang bagi penjawat awam dan pelepasan cukai yang diperluas untuk penjagaan selepas bersalin.

Bagaimanapun, Lai berkata, belanjawan tersebut perlu menyediakan pembiayaan khusus dan mampan bagi mangsa terselamat keganasan berasaskan jantina, termasuk akses kepada perkhidmatan sokongan, petugas barisan hadapan yang terlatih secukupnya, kaunseling dan bantuan pemulihan jangka panjang.

“Mengambil kira kes-kes terkini di sekolah, belanjawan ini mesti memainkan peranan lebih tegas untuk membendung peningkatan keganasan terhadap murid perempuan, dengan komitmen lebih jelas terhadap pendidikan seksualiti komprehensif, program kesedaran, kaunseling mudah diakses, serta langkah pencegahan yang berkesan,” katanya.

Menyentuh soal penyertaan ekonomi golongan wanita, Lai berkata, kekangan struktur, khususnya beban tanggungjawab penjagaan yang tidak seimbang, terus menyekat akses mereka kepada pekerjaan yang wajar serta kebebasan kewangan, walaupun penglibatan wanita pada peringkat pendidikan tinggi kekal kukuh.

Walaupun mengalu-alukan pengiktirafan belanjawan terhadap ekonomi penjagaan, beliau berkata, perkhidmatan penjagaan komuniti yang berkualiti dan berpatutan masih amat diperlukan, di samping perlindungan serta sokongan lebih ampuh buat penjaga tidak bergaji.

Beliau turut menggesa kerajaan menyepadukan perspektif jantina dan ketidakupayaan ke dalam perbelanjaan awam bagi sektor pengangkutan, perumahan, penjagaan kesihatan serta perlindungan sosial, dengan tumpuan khusus diberikan kepada wanita luar bandar, isi rumah berpendapatan rendah, ibu tunggal, wanita migran, dan orang kurang upaya (OKU).

Sehubungan itu, Lai meminta kerajaan mewajibkan pelaksanaan pendekatan belanjawan responsif jantina merentas semua kementerian, beserta penyata belanjawan gender umum yang menggariskan peruntukan, penerima manfaat, sasaran yang boleh diukur, serta hasil akhir.

Beliau turut mencadangkan penerbitan penyata belanjawan jantina secara terbuka yang menyenaraikan pengagihan dana, kumpulan sasaran, matlamat terukur, dan keberhasilan inisiatif, diiringi pelaporan berkala mengenai sejauh mana perbelanjaan awam mampu merapatkan jurang ketidaksamarataan gender.
Menurutnya, Malaysia boleh mencontohi kerangka dasar negara-negara seperti Maghribi, Rwanda, Korea Selatan, dan Austria.

“Langkah-langkah sedemikian penting untuk memperkukuh akauntabiliti, menilai kesan sebenar perbelanjaan awam, serta memastikan setiap komitmen terhadap kesaksamaan jantina benar-benar diterjemahkan kepada perubahan bermakna dalam kehidupan wanita,” katanya.

74cc9b8338ef9a99: BATU PAHAT: A sombre mood enveloped Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital's Forensic Department here today as Hairul Aziah Rahmad arrived to claim the body of her daughter, who died in a fiery crash yesterday.
Overcome with grief, the 52-year-old woman had to be supported by family members as she repeatedly expressed her wish to see her daughter's face for the last time.
She said she had arrived too late at the accident scene at Batu 1, Jalan Yong Peng-Ayer Hitam, yesterday.
"When I arrived at the scene, all that was left of the car was its frame," she said when met at the hospital.
Her daughter, Siti Nurmaisarah Abd Jalil, 22, and her cousin, Siti Nur Batrisya Mohd Khalid, 22, died when their car caught fire following a collision with a lorry.
Hairul Aziah's sister-in-law, Zahrah Suliman, 61, said Siti Nurmaisarah had helped support the family since her parents separated, as her mother's health condition limited her ability to work.
"She was a good daughter and worked hard to support the family. She had planned to live with her family in a new house after getting married.
"She had told us that she wanted to bring us to live with her. She did so much to help the family, including taking care of her brother.
"But sadly, her dreams were not realised.
"That is what makes our family so heartbroken," she said.
Zahrah said she was looking for a new house so that Hairul Aziah and her brother, who is a person with disabilities, could live with her.
Siti Nurmaisarah had hoped to bring the family together under one roof after her marriage, but those hopes were cut short by the tragedy.
Meanwhile, Siti Nur Batrisya's mother, Hamidah Sulaiman, said her youngest child, who was affectionately known as 'adik', and Siti Nurmaisarah had been inseparable since childhood.
"Both of them loved cats and would feed those they came across. Sometimes, they would even bring the cats home," she said.
677a81cff53512e2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Khazanah Nasional Berhad today welcomed the Malaysia Madani Budget 2027, describing it as a people-centric blueprint that strengthens the country’s long-term competitiveness while addressing immediate concerns over the cost of living and wages.

In a statement following the tabling of the budget by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Khazanah managing director Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir said the spending plan arrived at a critical juncture as Malaysia navigates geopolitical uncertainty, supply chain disruptions and elevated fuel prices linked to the ongoing conflict in West Asia.

He said Budget 2027, themed “Malaysia MADANI: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi”, balances economic growth with inclusivity by focusing on strategic sectors such as semiconductors, energy transition, infrastructure, enterprise development and talent development.

According to Amirul Feisal, these priorities are essential for strengthening Malaysia’s industrial base, increasing economic complexity and creating higher-value opportunities for businesses and workers.
“Importantly, the Budget places emphasis not only on growth, but on quality growth,” he said.

Khazanah also welcomed measures aimed at ensuring broader participation in national development, including initiatives benefiting workers, youth, entrepreneurs, Bumiputera companies, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), and communities facing economic and climate-related challenges.

The sovereign wealth fund said it fully supports the government’s move to raise the living wage benchmark for employees of government-linked investment companies (GLICs) and government-linked companies (GLCs) to RM3,400 per month, in line with efforts to increase labour’s share of gross domestic product (GDP).

On heritage conservation, Amirul Feisal said Khazanah would continue restoration work under its Dana Warisan investments through the broader Warisan KL initiative, including ongoing projects at the Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad Complex and Carcosa.
Khazanah also announced a collaboration with the Penang and Selangor state governments to strengthen Malaysia’s semiconductor and advanced manufacturing ecosystem.
Under the initiative, Penang, Selangor and Khazanah will each contribute RM50 million to a Strategic Investment Fund, bringing the fund’s initial size to RM150 million.
The fund is aimed at supporting the growth of high-potential Malaysian companies, while complementing Budget 2027’s emphasis on vendor development, innovation and market expansion.
In support of Bumiputera business growth, Khazanah said Dana Ciptawan will be expanded to RM250 million in collaboration with Teraju to assist Bumiputera and Malaysian mid-tier companies.

The fund also welcomed government ambitions in energy transition and climate resilience, citing Tenaga Nasional Berhad’s investment in the national electricity grid and UEM Lestra’s RM1 billion renewable energy investment as key enablers of Malaysia’s energy security, affordability and sustainability agenda.

Amirul Feisal said Khazanah remains committed to supporting national development through initiatives such as Dana Impak, Jelawang Capital, Dana Ciptawan, Dana Warisan, K-Youth, Bakat Madani and Yayasan Hasanah.

He said the organisation would continue working with other GLICs under the Ministry of Finance’s GEAR-uP programme to mobilise capital through disciplined investments, catalytic partnerships and impact-driven programmes that contribute to Malaysia’s long-term competitiveness.
1cf09dedac2c4198: SINGAPORE, Oct 10 — A fragrance shop along Bussorah Street has shared CCTV footage of a woman allegedly stealing a bottle of fragrance from its display, with the incident drawing calls from netizens for her and her partner to be held accountable.

984168e976da21e0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi was accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara on Saturday on the occasion of his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming office in June 2014, at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
Sultan Ibrahim graciously welcomed the arrival of El-Sisi at 10.08 am.

Also in attendance were Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, and Investment, Trade, and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
Following the welcoming ceremony, El-Sisi inspected a guard of honour comprising 28 officers and personnel from the First Battalion of the Royal Ranger Regiment.

The welcoming ceremony at the Istana Negara parade square began with a rendition of the national anthems of both countries by the Royal Ranger Regiment band led by Captain (DOM) Mohd Fahmy Harun, followed by a 21-gun salute by the 41st Battery of the Royal Artillery Regiment.

The Egyptian president then inspected a guard of honour comprising five officers and 89 personnel from the three branches of the Malaysian Armed Forces, namely the Malaysian Army, the Royal Malaysian Navy, and the Royal Malaysian Air Force, led by Major Muhammad Waqiyudin Abd Rahman.
His Majesty then grants an audience to El-Sisi and the Egyptian delegation and witnessed a presentation of royal tokens of appreciation ceremony at Dewan Seri Maharaja.
Sultan Ibrahim then hosted a state banquet at the Grand Banquet Hall in honour of El-Sisi and the Egyptian government delegation.

El-Sisi’s visit is the first by an Egyptian president to Malaysia for nearly three decades. The last visit, by former President Mohamed Hosni Mubarak, took place in November 1997 when he attended the G-15 Summit in Kuala Lumpur. Mubarak also undertook an official visit as the Egyptian Vice President in 1979.

Wisma Putra in a statement on Friday said El-Sisi, who is accompanied by Cabinet ministers and senior Egyptian government officials, is also scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting Anwar Ibrahim to take stock of progress in bilateral cooperation and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest.

Both leaders will then witness the exchange of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) between Malaysia and Egypt, followed by an official hi-tea at Seri Perdana Complex hosted by the prime minister at Seri Perdana Complex.
Malaysia and Egypt have established diplomatic relations since 1959.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia’s seventh largest trading partner in Africa.
Malaysia’s total trade with Egypt was valued at RM3.08 billion (US$720 million), with exports valued at RM2.55 billion (US$600 million) and imports at RM530 million (US$120 million).
From January to August 2026, total trade between the two countries increased by 74.7 per cent to RM3.49 billion (US$870 million). — Bernama
