"Immediate repairs are needed as this is the main route for residents commuting and sending their children to school. There are also concerns that the sinkhole could expand to the adjacent road," he said.
6a34be4a63dc6281: KUALA LUMPUR: The absence of a dedicated allocation for Harimau Malaya in the 2027 Budget raises fresh questions about how Malaysian football will finance its national team and development programmes, as the government shifts towards broader sports funding frameworks.

For years, Malaysian football has received direct government support, but the returns on that investment have remained a subject of debate, with the national team yet to make a breakthrough in World Cup/Asian Cup qualification and youth sides continuing to face stiff competition from regional rivals.
Under the 2025 Budget, Putrajaya allocated RM15 million specifically for Harimau Malaya and its youth development squads in collaboration with the FA of Malaysia (FAM).

The funding was subsequently doubled to RM30 million through a public-private matching mechanism to strengthen administrative governance and technical development, following an earlier RM5 million government allocation after Malaysia's 3-3 draw against South Korea at the 2023 Asian Cup.

Despite the funding, Malaysia have yet to translate their investment into a breakthrough in World Cup qualification, while questions remain over the long-term development of the national team's talent pipeline.
In the 2027 Budget, neither Harimau Malaya nor FAM was named in a dedicated allocation, with sports funding instead channelled through broader programmes.
When asked how the absence of an earmarked grant would affect its operations and development plans heading into 2027, FAM said it respected the government's priorities.

"The FAM respects the government's priorities in framing the Budget and hopes that support for the development of national football can be sustained through close cooperation with the Youth and Sports Ministry and relevant agencies," the national body said in response to queries.

FAM also said it would prioritise programmes according to its available finances while seeking greater backing from corporate partners and the private sector "to ensure the continuous development of national football."

The government's RM27 million allocation for school sports activities also places renewed emphasis on grassroots participation, potentially complementing the work of national sports associations in identifying and developing young talent.
However, the extent to which this funding will benefit football specifically remains unclear, as the allocation is intended to support school sports activities more broadly.

When asked how much funding it anticipates receiving from the RM460 million sports development allocation and the RM240 million SEA Games fund, FAM said it had yet to establish an estimate because the distribution mechanism and specific allocation for football had not been detailed.

"In the meantime, FAM has not set any estimate of the funding to be received from the government in preparation for the 2027 SEA Games, given that the distribution mechanism and specific allocation for football have yet to be detailed," the national body said.
Nevertheless, FAM said it would continue engaging with the relevant authorities to ensure the national Under-23 squad's preparation requirements were considered ahead of the regional competition.

"FAM will continue to work closely with the ministry and relevant agencies to ensure that the preparation needs of the national football squad ahead of the 2027 SEA Games receive due consideration," the FAM said.
a77e9d01dc938aa0: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim held a four-eyed meeting with Egyptian president Abdel Fattah El-Sisi at the Seri Perdana Complex here today, marking a significant step towards elevating Malaysia-Egypt relations to a strategic partnership after more than six decades of diplomatic ties.

The meeting, held in conjunction with El-Sisi’s two-day state visit to Malaysia, provided an opportunity for both leaders to review bilateral cooperation, explore new areas of collaboration, and exchange views on regional and international developments of mutual interest.

El-Sisi, who is on his first state visit to Malaysia since assuming office in June 2014, will take part in a series of official engagements aimed at strengthening political, economic and diplomatic relations between the two nations.

Anwar and El-Sisi are scheduled to lead bilateral discussions involving delegations from both countries, focusing on expanding cooperation in key sectors, particularly trade, investment and economic development.

A key highlight of the engagements is the proposed elevation of bilateral relations to that of a strategic partnership, reflecting the shared commitment of Malaysia and Egypt to advancing cooperation to a higher level.
Both leaders were also scheduled to witness the exchange of memoranda of understanding, aimed at further strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

A joint press conference is scheduled to follow the bilateral discussions, during which Anwar and El-Sisi were expected to outline the outcomes of their engagements and the future direction of Malaysia-Egypt relations.
The high-level engagement comes amid growing economic ties between Malaysia and Egypt, with bilateral trade surging 74.7% to RM3.49 billion in the first eight months of 2026.
The figure has already exceeded the RM3.08 billion recorded for the whole of 2025, highlighting the expanding trade relationship and growing economic potential between the two countries.
In 2025, Egypt was Malaysia’s seventh-largest trading partner in Africa, with Malaysian exports valued at RM2.55 billion, while imports amounted to RM530 million.

Malaysia and Egypt established diplomatic relations in 1959 and have maintained longstanding cooperation in various fields, including education, trade and investment, alongside close engagement on regional and international platforms.

El-Sisi’s state visit, undertaken at the invitation of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, is expected to open a new chapter in bilateral relations and provide fresh momentum for stronger strategic and economic cooperation between the two nations.
37c326687bc4a542: IPOH: A man lost about RM12.47 million after his crypto assets were believed to have been stolen through unauthorised access to his digital wallet.
Perak police chief Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 38-year-old victim realised this yesterday afternoon while he was in Teluk Intan.
He said the victim realised that a sum of his crypto assets had been transferred out of his digital wallet without his knowledge or consent.
“A preliminary investigation found that the transaction involved the transfer of crypto assets through a blockchain network.

“Police are conducting further investigations to identify those involved and track the flow of transactions with assistance from the Bukit Aman commercial crime investigation department’s crypto unit,” he said in a statement today.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine, upon conviction.

Alwi advised the public to be careful about phishing and online scams, avoid clicking on suspicious links, always monitor their digital wallet transactions, act immediately if they suspect their accounts have been hacked, and strengthen their digital security measures.
12d1b42fb7d0267e: KUALA LUMPUR: Despite showing early promise during qualifying, Moto3 rookie Hakim Danish Ramli will start from 18th place on the grid for tomorrow's Grand Prix of Indonesia.

The AEON Credit-MT Helmets-MSI rider did well to place second in qualifying one (Q1) after clocking one minute, 37.980 seconds at the Mandalika circuit earlier today, which allowed him to progress to Q2.
The 19-year-old, however, could not replicate his pace in the faster Q2 group and was forced to settle for 18th on 1:39.619s.
Red Bull KTM Ajo's Brian Uriarte, Danish's old rival from the Red Bull Rookies Cup series, took pole on a solid 1:36.861s.
Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP's David Almansa (+0.087s) was a close second while Uriarte's teammate Alvaro Carpe (+0.156s) rounded out the front row.
Danish did well to finish third at Mugello and clinch his maiden GP win at Brno in June but his form has tapered since the summer break.
fe9ffe5763a8a1c1: NEW DELHI, Oct 10 — Indian police detained the head of the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) online movement today ahead of a major protest it called against the Election Commission, the party said.

Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital New Delhi, where the demonstration was due to take place, the youth-led CJP said in a social media post.
The protests are the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision by the Election Commission of India (ECI).
Opposition parties and critics say the revision could disenfranchise millions of voters and benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety in the “special intensive revision”, saying it was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.
“It’s official... we are living under an absolute dictatorship ruled by Modi,” Arvind Kejriwal of the opposition Aam Aadmi Party said in a statement.
“Arresting cockroaches straight off their flight shows an unprecedented level of fear.”

Delhi has been under a strict security clampdown since yesterday, with tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel deployed to stop those seeking to reach the main protest site in the heart of the capital.
Authorities have closed dozens of metro stations, cancelled several trains coming to Delhi and shut down mobile internet temporarily around the protest site.
Television images today showed police chasing down several protesters and hauling them into vehicles in areas around central Delhi.
More than 200 protesters have been detained so far, local media reports said.
The protests are widely seen as a reprise of CJP’s mass mobilisation in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal.
This time, they are demanding ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar resign from his post. — AFP
d480e4629e6468ff: PETALING JAYA: Tabung pos kerajaan bagi memastikan perkhidmatan penghantaran pos dan bungkusan terus sampai ke kawasan luar bandar serta pedalaman akan direalisasikan menerusi suntikan dana sebanyak RM150 juta pada suku pertama 2027.

Menteri Komunikasi Fahmi Fadzil berkata, tabung yang diuruskan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM) itu akan membantu menyokong urusan penghantaran ke kawasan yang kurang mendapat liputan.

“Walaupun tabung ini sudah lama ada dalam Akta (Perkhidmatan Pos), sejak 2012, namun tidak pernah ada kerajaan sebelum ini yang berusaha untuk mewujudkannya," katanya pada sambutan Hari Pos Sedunia hari ini.
Fahmi berkata, operasi tabung tersebut menggunakan prinsip yang sama dengan Tabung Pemberian Perkhidmatan Sejagat (USP) dalam sektor telekomunikasi yang menyediakan kemudahan ke kawasan terpencil.

Beliau turut memaklumkan bahawa SKMM telah diminta memastikan peruntukan berkenaan tidak hanya terhad kepada perkhidmatan pos tradisional, sebaliknya turut merangkumi penghantaran barangan dan bungkusan ke kawasan terlibat.

Selain itu, Fahmi menegaskan kerajaan sedang meneliti hala tuju jangka panjang industri pos dan kurier, khususnya ketika kepesatan e-dagang serta kemasukan syarikat kurier asing terus mengubah lanskap sektor berkenaan.
Justeru, penyesuaian terhadap dasar, undang-undang, dan operasi sedia ada mungkin diperlukan bagi membantu industri menyesuaikan diri dengan cabaran semasa.
c5e53e93d615e5ca: KUALA LUMPUR: Though painful, families of missing Malaysians are prepared to accept Nepal's proposal to shorten the period for declaring missing disaster victims dead.
Sivakumar Kalimuthu, 63, acknowledged he had to accept the proposal by the Nepali government to shorten the declaration period to 45 days from 12 years.
Sivakumar, whose wife, Kalai Mathe Karuppaiah, 57, is missing, said the Malaysian government has not issued any official notification regarding the proposal so far.
"We have to accept it because the incident has already happened and we have no direct line of communication with them to voice feedback to the Nepali government.
"We were previously told that death certificates are usually issued after seven years if victims remain missing, though in this case, the period was shortened to three years.
"Nepal's decision on the proposal may make it easier for us to transfer the victim's assets to other family members," he said when contacted today.

Sharing a similar sentiment, Hani Othman, wife of Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, admitted it was difficult to accept the decision since no alternatives were provided to next of kin.
"I have mixed feelings about accepting any decision regarding Nepal's proposal.
"However, as next of kin, we have to accept whatever the government decides.
"I only learned about this through social media and am still unsure of the exact decision regarding the proposal," she said.
Meanwhile, efforts to obtain a response from the Malaysian government regarding the proposal remain ongoing, with the Foreign Ministry reportedly reviewing the recommendation.
Yesterday, Nepal reportedly proposed shortening the current 12-year missing period for declaring victims dead to 45 days.
Kathmandu proposed this following devastating floods in Nepal that claimed numerous lives from various nations.
Nepal was struck on Aug 26 by a disaster described as a Himalayan Tsunami following rockfalls and snow avalanches, which killed more than 1,400 people and left over 6,000 untraceable.
Search, rescue, and recovery operations remain underway in several flood-affected areas following widespread destruction that left over 70,000 residents directly affected and displaced.
During the floods, settlements on high-altitude slopes near the Tibet border were severely impacted by swift floodwaters following a sudden glacial lake outburst.
2fe6d465389e8ca8: TAIPEI, Oct 10 — Taiwan aims to “deter war” by increasing its defence spending, the democratic island’s leader said today, as China uses military pressure to assert its territorial claims.
Taiwan’s 23 million people live under the constant threat of an attack by China, which insists the island is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex it.
“Our aim by increasing investment in national defence is not to provoke, rather, it is to deter war,” President Lai Ching-te said in a speech to celebrate Taiwan’s National Day.

Successive administrations have ramped up military spending as Taiwan improves its fighting abilities to avoid a potential Chinese invasion—and to show the United States it is serious about its own defence.
Lai’s government has earmarked a record NT$1.1 trillion (RM140 billion) in defence spending for 2027, which accounts for more than three per cent of GDP.

“We do not seek hegemony, nor do we seek to dominate others,” Lai said in his annual address in front of the Presidential Office in Taipei, where thousands of people, including foreign diplomats, were gathered.

“However, peace cannot rely solely on wishes, and tolerance cannot become a pretext for aggressors to encroach ever further,” Lai said, noting that China continued to “apply pressure through military and grey-zone activities in an attempt to alter the status quo across the Taiwan Strait”.
Lai welcomed talks between the United States and China, but insisted “there must be respect for the right of the people of Taiwan to exist”.
Government officials in Washington and Taipei have said repeatedly that US policy on Taiwan has not changed under President Donald Trump, whose remarks have jangled nerves at times.
‘US support is extremely important’
The United States switched official diplomatic relations from Taipei to Beijing nearly 50 years ago, but Washington is Taipei’s most important security backer.
Trump’s suggestion in May, following a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, that US arms sales to Taiwan could be a bargaining chip with China set off alarm bells across the world.
Taiwan is waiting for Trump’s signature on US$14 billion (RM57 billion) worth of weapons, including the US-made Patriot air defence system.

Taiwanese fighter jets and two Chinook helicopters carrying giant Taiwan flags flew over the capital ahead of Lai’s wide-ranging speech, which also covered housing pressure and the declining population.
“You can really feel the warmth in Taiwanese society,” said Feng Jing-heng, 70, who was in the crowd watching the military parade and dance performances.
Tao Yi-feng, a political scientist at National Taiwan University, said Lai’s speech was “relatively moderate” and unlikely to be met with “overt reaction from Beijing”.
Today’s celebrations mark the 115th anniversary of the toppling of China’s Qing dynasty and the subsequent founding of the Republic of China.

The current dispute between China and Taiwan dates to a civil war between the nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek, who retreated to the island in 1949 after being defeated by Mao Zedong’s communist fighters.

Parliamentary speaker Han Kuo-yu, who is a senior member of the main opposition party that favours closer ties with China, said “US support is extremely important to Taiwan’s security”, but he noted the historical and cultural links with China.
“The overwhelming majority of Taiwanese compatriots do not want war; they wish to live their lives in peace and hope for peaceful cross-strait exchanges,” Han said at the National Day event. — AFP
0ca2bbc903e51a01: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Malaysia is still awaiting a response through official diplomatic channels on arrangements for its offer of firefighting assistance to Indonesia, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
Fahmi, who is also the government spokesperson, said discussions had taken place directly between the countries’ leaders and expressed hope that their good relations would allow follow-up action.

“I believe that the matter has been conveyed, that discussions have taken place directly with the Indonesian president, and we believe that the good relations today will make it possible for follow-up action to be taken.
“However, so far (as of this morning) no response has been conveyed through Wisma Putra.
“We will wait a little longer,” Fahmi told a press conference after officiating the World Post Day at the Pos Malaysia headquarters here today.
Fahmi was responding to reporters who asked for an update of efforts taken to improve air quality in Malaysia.
He added that current and immediate measures such as temporary shutting schools and postponing school Sports Day were among other actions taken.
“Similarly for other sectors, keep a lookout on updates from respective ministries on next course of action, he said.
Indonesia had earlier agreed to Malaysia’s offer of assistance during Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s meeting with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto in September.

Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said on October 7 that the two countries were still negotiating operational arrangements, including how the mission would be carried out and where the Malaysian team would be deployed.

Malaysia’s proposed assistance includes a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 officers and personnel from the National Disaster Management Agency, Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and Royal Malaysian Air Force.
2dbed29c2e1e54b9: SINGAPORE, Oct 10 — Singapore is ready to assist Indonesia amid worsening haze conditions in the region.

Speaking to the media today, Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu revealed that she has been in contact with her Indonesian counterpart and has offered support in managing forest fires, which have been made increasingly difficult to put out due to dry weather brought on by El Nino.
“We are aware that efforts are going on. We stand ready to assist where we can.”
The minister also expressed appreciation for Indonesia’s efforts to contain the fires, adding that Singapore supports any further regional discussions and co-operation on the transboundary haze.
Meanwhile, the haze in Singapore has worsened over the past week, with Fu attributing the deterioration to an increase in hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan, as well as unfavourable wind conditions.
While some rain is expected over the weekend, she warned that the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) could still exceed 200, entering the very unhealthy range.
‘We are very concerned about public health,” said Fu, highlighting vulnerable groups such as seniors, young children, pregnant women and those with heart or lung conditions.
However, the minister assured Singaporeans that the government is closely monitoring the situation, with the Haze Task Force meeting regularly to prepare for any further deterioration.
Among the measures in place is the distribution of N95 masks to eligible Singaporeans when the 24-hour PSI exceeds 200.
They can be collected at vending machines or community clubs when necessary.

Those eligible include Singaporeans from the Pioneer Generation, Merdeka Generation, holders of the Community Health Assistance Scheme (CHAS) Blue and Orange cards, medical fee exemption card, as well as recipients of ComCare Assistance.
Pregnant women and children between ages seven and 16, and those with medical conditions such as asthma, may also collect their masks at People’s Association venues.
Air-conditioned areas in Community Clubs (CC) and selected Residents’ Committee and Residents’ Network centres will also be activated as haze shelters.
These would provide relief for residents without air-conditioning at home, allowing them to seek shelter in air-conditioned areas with air purifiers.
Reiterating the government’s commitment to protecting Singaporeans, Fu said contingency plans have been drawn up for different PSI levels.
Sector-specific guidance is also available for schools, including preschools, workplaces and healthcare institutions, with measures adjusted according to the severity of the haze.

Preschools, for instance, will suspend outdoor activities and strenuous indoor activities if air quality reaches the very unhealthy range, according to a joint statement by the National Environment Agency and 28 government agencies on Friday.
“We are on top of the situation. We have plans put in place, and we’ll do whatever is needed to protect the public health of Singaporeans,” said Fu. — AsiaOne
cbee2eded05b0b10: ISTANBUL: Tiga terbunuh dalam dua serangan pada Khamis ke atas Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Raja Khalid di ibu negara Riyadh dan sebuah pesawat Saudia Airlines, menurut Arab Saudi pada Jumaat, lapor Anadolu Ajansi.
Menurut Pihak Berkuasa Am Penerbangan Awam dalam kenyataan di X, serangan pertama menyasarkan kemudahan lapangan terbang manakala serangan kedua mengena pesawat milik syarikat penerbangan negara itu.
Pasukan tindak balas kecemasan pantas bertindak balas terhadap serangan yang turut mencederakan 'sebilangan rakyat dan penduduk pelbagai negara,' kata pihak berkuasa.
Mangsa yang sebahagiannya parah segera dibawa ke hospital untuk rawatan, menurut kenyataan itu, sambil menambah bahawa serangan juga menyebabkan beberapa kerosakan material.
Pegawai turut mengumumkan penyambungan semula aktiviti operasi di lapangan terbang dan trafik udara.
Penyiar milik kerajaan TV Al Ekhbariya melaporkan operasi di lapangan terbang itu disambung semula setakat 6 petang waktu tempatan (1500 GMT) pada Khamis.

Dalam satu kenyataan berasingan, Saudia Airlines mengesahkan bahawa insiden itu 'menyebabkan kerosakan pada salah satu pesawatnya semasa ia berada di landasan lapangan terbang' sambil menambah bahawa tiada penumpang di dalam pesawat ketika kejadian.
Serangan menyebabkan seorang kakitangan maut, kata syarikat penerbangan itu sambil menyampaikan ucapan takziah kepada keluarga mangsa yang dikenal pasti sebagai Kapten Hamoud Ali Alkalthami.
Syarikat penerbangan berkenaan menyatakan penghargaan serta mengiktiraf sumbangan beliau.

Pihak berkuasa Arab Saudi tidak menyatakan siapa yang bertanggungjawab terhadap serangan pelanggaran itu namun ia berlaku di tengah-tengah peningkatan semula pertempuran antara tentera kerajaan Yaman dan Houthi.
5a3b0517c5301c49: PENSACOLA: Hurricane Isaias weakened to a Category 1 storm on Friday, rapidly lost wind speed after hitting the Florida coast, the US National Hurricane Center said while warning of storm surges and snapped power lines as it moves through the Deep South.

The hurricane, crossing the western Florida Panhandle after making landfall near Destin as a Category 2 storm, was about 105km west-northwest of Panama City, Florida, packing maximum sustained winds of 150 kph, the NHC said in an advisory.

The centre warned of possible storm surges, urban and river flooding and flash floods across the region, with considerable impacts likely across much of southern Alabama and the Florida Panhandle into southwest Georgia.
Isaias, the first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season, is expected to continue weakening but produce gusty winds well inland through Saturday even after it becomes post-tropical, the NHC said.
Alabama's emergency management agency said the hurricane has downed trees and power lines, making travel hazardous in Houston County, which is under a flash flood warning.

"Due to the impacts of Hurricane Isaias, all Houston County roads are closed until further notice," it posted on X. "These road closures will remain in effect until conditions are deemed safe for travel."
Isaias is expected to cross Alabama and go into the Tennessee Valley over the weekend, the NHC said.
President Donald Trump, asked about hurricane preparations, told reporters outside the White House, "We're watching it very closely, the hurricane," adding that it was "under control."
More than 412,000 people in Florida and nearly 243,000 in Alabama lost power as the storm hit shore, according to power outage tracking firm PowerOutage.us.
"Emergency declarations have been approved in Florida and Alabama to ensure federal resources are available to respond to Isaias," homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said on X.
Florida's emergency services urged residents to shelter in place and watch for hurricane conditions across the north of the state.
eb93074295651663: SINGAPORE, Oct 10 — Two men, aged 35 and 39, were yesterday arrested for alleged criminal trespass after they allegedly entered the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix (SGP) event area without valid tickets.
Police said in a statement this morning that they received a report that a man had been detained by SGP staff within the event area along Temasek Boulevard at about 3pm yesterday.
Preliminary investigations later showed that two men — who are acquainted — had attempted to enter the event area along Temasek Avenue at about 1.45pm without valid tickets.
The 35-year-old man was denied entry at the entrance after his ticket was found to be invalid, while the 39-year-old man managed to enter the event area despite holding an invalid ticket.
He is said to have subsequently gained unauthorised access to a restricted area meant for SGP staff and performing artistes.
Staff members later located the man and detained him within the event area. He was handed over to the police and arrested at the scene.
Meanwhile, the 35-year-old man was subsequently arrested by the police along Temasek Boulevard.
The 39-year-old man will be charged in court today with criminal trespass, an offence which carries a fine of up to S$1,500 (RM4,785), jail of up to three months, or both.
Investigations into the 35-year-old man are still ongoing.
The police said they take a serious view of unauthorised entry into restricted areas at major events, as such acts may compromise the safety and security of the event.
“Members of the public should comply with all access control measures by event organisers and only enter areas for which they have valid authorisation.
“Offenders will be dealt with firmly in accordance with the law,” they added. — AsiaOne
a3e35ae1f70a4241: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Love was in the air high above Kuala Lumpur this morning as Muar MP Syed Saddiq Abdul Rahman and singer-actress Bella Astillah officially became husband and wife in a romantic solemnisation ceremony at Merdeka 118.
The couple, affectionately known to fans as BASS — a combination of the initials of their names, Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq — got engaged on March 28.
They tied the knot in front of family, friends and political heavyweights, becoming the first to hold a wedding ceremony at the iconic skyscraper.

At exactly 10.40am, their marriage was declared sah (valid) after Syed Saddiq presented Bella with a mas kahwin (marriage dowry) of RM500, marking a new chapter in a romance that has captured the attention of Malaysians.
The celebrations began early, with guests dressed in white gathering at Park Hyatt Kuala Lumpur, located within Merdeka 118, from as early as 8am.
The wedding, inspired by Arabian elements and featuring an elegant white theme, was expected to welcome approximately 255 guests.

Among the notable faces in attendance were former health minister Khairy Jamaluddin, former prime ministers Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, and former deputy prime minister Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail.

The celebrity guest list included Bella’s close friends, Malaysian actress and former model Toh Puan Syamim Freida and Indonesian actress Tya Arifin, alongside actor Azad Jasmin and comedian and television presenter Nabil Ahmad.
The ceremony unfolded on the building’s 118th floor, with thousands of Malaysians tuning in to watch the much-anticipated union ‘live’ across platforms operated by pay-TV broadcaster Astro.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Syed Saddiq slips a ring onto Bella Astillah’s finger during their wedding ceremony at Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur October 10, 2026. — Picture courtesy of Astro

Syed Saddiq made his entrance alongside his parents at approximately 10.12am, before the ceremonial exchange of hantaran (wedding gifts), with seven trays presented by the groom’s side and nine by the bride’s.

Syed Saddiq’s gifts to his bride included RM100,000 in Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings through the i-Simpan facility, an umrah package and a scholarship for Bella to pursue a master’s degree in communication at Taylor’s University.

He also presented her with a home gym, massage chair and road bicycle, as well as insurance protection for Bella and her two children, Mohamad Ayden Adrean and Ara Adreanna, according to Astro Gempak.
Among the more sentimental gifts was a specially crafted gold piece depicting Mount Kinabalu, where Syed Saddiq proposed to Bella in March.
Bella, meanwhile, reciprocated with a customised gold ring, a pair of Christian Louboutin shoes, a Quran and perfume, according to Astro Awani.
She also presented him with a specially commissioned Iron Man-themed gold piece and an entry to a triathlon, reflecting his passion for endurance sports.
All eyes then turned to Bella as she made her entrance at around 10.28am, accompanied by her mother Siti Zarina Astillah, to the song Sampai Jadi Debu.
Both bride and groom wore outfits designed by Zaimi Zulkafli, with their wedding looks adding to the romantic elegance of the occasion.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Syed Saddiq and Bella Astillah pictured during their solemnisation ceremony at Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur October 10, 2026. — Picture courtesy of Astro
The solemnisation was officiated by former Federal Territories Mufti Datuk Seri Zulkifli Mohamad al-Bakri, with Bella’s father, Awang Astillah Abdullah, acting as her wali (marriage guardian).

Following the declaration of their marriage, Syed Saddiq recited the taklik, a declaration outlining conditions attached to the marriage under Islamic law, before the newlyweds exchanged rings and posed for photographs with family members and guests.
Speaking after the solemnisation, an overjoyed Syed Saddiq thanked those who had supported the couple throughout their relationship.
“Thank you for always praying for our journey,” he said.
“There were times when we faced obstacles and challenges, but I believe that through all your prayers, we have finally been brought together, from work partners to life partners.
“Alhamdulillah,” he added.
Bella, whose full name is Dayang Ara Nabellah Awang Astillah, was equally thankful that the ceremony had gone smoothly, expressing her appreciation to everyone who had supported the couple.
“We are truly grateful and appreciate all the support.”
“Alhamdulillah,” she said.
But beyond the star-studded guest list and romantic setting, some of the day’s most heartwarming moments came from the couple’s families, particularly Bella’s children, Ayden and Ara.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Guests at Syed Saddiq and Bella Astillah’s solemnisation ceremony at Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur October 10, 2026. — Picture courtesy of Astro
In a video shared by Astro Gempak ahead of the ceremony, Ayden expressed his excitement at welcoming a new member into the family and having someone he could call “Daddy”.
Ara was equally delighted at the prospect of having a new father figure in her life.

Syed Saddiq’s elder brother, Syed Abdullah Syed Abdul Rahman, better known as social media personality Space Dollah and a vocal supporter of the couple’s romance, also shared his excitement about becoming an uncle to Bella’s children.
“I want to make sure Ara and Ayden become legends,” he said.
And while the couple are now officially husband and wife, the wedding celebrations are far from over.

b292b29bfa38e969: PETALING JAYA: Usaha memartabatkan bahasa Melayu perlu disesuaikan dengan teknologi moden seperti kecerdasan buatan (AI) dan bukannya sekadar bergantung kepada nostalgia lalu, kata Ismail Sabri Yaakob.
Menurut bekas perdana menteri itu, bahasa Melayu mesti hadir dalam ruang teknologi yang membentuk kehidupan manusia masa kini agar ia terus berkembang dan kekal relevan di peringkat global.

Katanya, jika masyarakat mahu bahasa Melayu terus mempunyai tempat pada masa hadapan, pembangunan korpus bahasa, pangkalan data digital, dan teknologi pemprosesan bahasa yang berupaya memahami bahasa Melayu dengan baik perlu disegerakan.

"Bahasa yang hidup ialah bahasa yang berkembang bersama masyarakatnya. Oleh itu, bahasa Melayu perlu terus diperkaya dengan istilah baharu, karya baharu dan pemikiran baharu supaya mampu menjawab perubahan dalam kehidupan manusia.

"Dalam bidang sains dan teknologi misalnya, perkembangan kecerdasan buatan, bioteknologi, ekonomi digital dan teknologi maklumat memerlukan istilah, bahan rujukan serta kandungan ilmiah yang mampu memperkayakan bahasa kita," katanya ketika merasmikan Simposium Antarabangsa Aspirasi Bahasa Melayu (SAABM) Kali Ke-5 di Kuala Lumpur.
Tambahnya, pemeliharaan bahasa Melayu perlu bermula dari rumah dan sistem pendidikan bagi membina keyakinan generasi muda terhadap nilai serta keindahan bahasa berkenaan.
Mengulas lanjut, Ismail berkata kekuatan rantau Nusantara seperti kerjasama antara Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei, dan Singapura perlu dimanfaatkan.
Katanya, jalinan kerjasama dalam bidang pendidikan, penyelidikan, penerbitan, serta platform digital membolehkan karya dan pemikiran tempatan diketengahkan ke peringkat dunia.
Dalam pada itu, beliau berkata usaha memartabatkan bahasa Melayu tidak bermakna menutup pintu kepada bahasa asing.

"Penguasaan bahasa asing juga penting. Memartabatkan bahasa Melayu tidak bermaksud kita menolak bahasa lain, kerana keterbukaan kepada bahasa dan ilmu dunia akan memberikan kita lebih banyak ruang untuk memperkenalkan bahasa serta budaya sendiri.
"Kita mahu generasi yang kukuh jati dirinya dalam bahasa Melayu, tetapi pada masa yang sama mampu berkomunikasi dan bersaing dalam masyarakat antarabangsa," katanya.
bc4b4bb19f871864: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The government has allocated RM150 million to activate the Postal Service Fund, which is now expected to begin operating in the first quarter of 2027, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the initial fund will, among other things, support the Universal Service Obligation (USO), particularly the delivery of letters to rural areas, remote locations and islands.

“The government has agreed to activate the Postal Fund, which will hopefully begin operating in the first quarter of 2027, with initial funding of RM150 million,” Fahmi told a press conference after officiating the World Post Day celebration at the Pos Malaysia headquarters here today.
Fahmi had previously said in January that the government was targeting the fund’s introduction by the third quarter of 2026.
The RM150 million allocation is three times the RM50 million funding previously announced for the programme.

Acknowledging the changing landscape of e-commerce and digital technology, Fahmi said this also meant that adjustments might be needed to policies, legislation and operational practices governing the postal sector.
He stressed that the welfare of postal and courier workers must also be protected, including ensuring fair compensation and decent wages.
“We do not want a situation where there is excessive imbalance,” he said.
He added that MCMC had begun engagement with e-commerce service providers, with discussions to be extended to major courier companies.

The commission would also continue discussions with regulatory agencies, including the Royal Malaysia Police and the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency, to address complaints involving e-commerce transactions and parcel deliveries.
Fahmi said the Postal Service Fund had been provided for under legislation since 2012, but previous governments had not taken steps to operationalise it.
He said he had also asked that the fund’s scope not be limited to conventional postal services, noting that deliveries of goods to remote communities could also serve an important function.
“MCMC will make a full announcement in due course to explain the functions of the Postal Fund,” he added.
The Postal Service Fund was provided for under Section 98 of the Postal Services Act 2012, which places it under MCMC’s control and operation.
Section 98 also explained how the fund is to comprise money provided by Parliament and contributions from licensees or other parties.
Under this provision, it also permits spending on universal postal services, expanding and improving the postal network, technology and other postal-related purposes determined by the minister.

In-line with the World Post Day, Fahmi said the Communications Ministry, MCMC and Pos Malaysia would work together on special initiatives to mark the 70th anniversary of National Postal Day, including efforts to strengthen ties between Pos Malaysia and the Malaysian Philatelic Society.
987d3293f6bd9c36: SINGAPORE, Oct 10 — European authorities have recalled Fromagerie Gillot raw milk cheese products from France due to the potential presence of Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC).

The recall is ongoing, added SFA.
STEC infection can occur by consuming contaminated food, particularly raw or unpasteurised milk and its products.
Food contaminated with the toxin may not look or smell spoilt but can cause serious infections.
Symptoms of STEC infection can include diarrhoea, stomach cramps, and vomiting.
Consumers who have purchased the affected products are advised not to consume them.
Those who have already eaten the products and have concerns about their health should seek medical advice.
Consumers may also contact their point of purchase for more information. — AsiaOne

8e7b4b3123edbcf6: PETALING JAYA: The All Women’s Action Society (Awam) has urged MPs to scrutinise the 2027 budget through a gender lens when Parliament debates the allocations in the coming weeks, saying they fall short of addressing longstanding issues affecting women.

Awam president Lai Suat Yan said the budget made some improvements, including extra aid for care work, better maternity leave entitlement, and upgrades to childcare facilities at government premises, but remained “largely a disappointment".
Lai said the budget failed to adequately address issues such as gender-based violence, low workforce participation, and unequal burden of unpaid care work.
"Many longstanding needs of Malaysian women remain unmet, and this will continue to have implications for women’s rights, safety and well-being in the coming year," she said in a statement today.

"Women remain far from achieving equality and parity and, therefore, Awam maintains that public budgeting must be viewed through a gender-responsive lens to ensure that public resources address existing inequalities, respond to the diverse needs of women and contribute to an inclusive and sustainable national development."

Under the 2027 budget tabled on Oct 9, several targeted initiatives and benefits for women were included, such as longer maternity leave for civil servants and expanded tax relief for postpartum care.

However, Lai said the budget needed to provide dedicated and sustainable funding for survivors of gender-based violence, including access to support services, adequately trained frontline responders, counselling and long-term recovery assistance.

"With the recent cases in schools, the budget must do more to address rising violence against girls in schools, with clearer commitments to comprehensive sexuality education, awareness programmes, accessible counselling and effective prevention measures," she said.

On women’s economic participation, Lai said structural barriers, particularly unequal care responsibilities, continued to limit women’s access to decent employment and financial independence despite their strong participation in higher education.

While acknowledging the budget’s recognition of the care economy, she said more affordable, quality community-based care services were needed, alongside stronger protections and support for unpaid caregivers.

She also urged the government to incorporate gender and disability perspectives into public spending on transport, housing, healthcare and social protection, with particular attention to rural women, low-income households, single mothers, migrant women and women with disabilities.

Lai called on the government to make gender-responsive budgeting mandatory across all ministries, with a public gender budget statement setting out allocations, beneficiaries, measurable targets and outcomes.

She proposed a publicly available gender budget statement outlining allocations, beneficiaries, measurable targets and outcomes, alongside regular reporting on how public expenditure addressed gender inequalities.
She said Malaysia could replicate the frameworks of countries such as Morocco, Rwanda, South Korea and Austria.

“Such measures are essential to strengthen accountability, assess the actual impact of public spending and ensure that commitments to gender equality translate into meaningful improvements in women’s lives,” she said.
48cc9a2c70eea42b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim today consented to the conferring of the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) award to Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, who is currently in Malaysia on a two-day state visit.

18cded191a5f4c44: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — The government’s increased allocation for healthcare under Budget 2027 is seen as a catalyst for Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) to upgrade its infrastructure and accelerate its transition to a fully digital hospital.

HKL director Datuk Dr Harikrishna K R Nair said the allocation would help the 156-year-old hospital modernise its electrical systems and other facilities, as well as strengthen its information technology infrastructure.

“We are quite happy because Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has increased the healthcare allocation by RM1.2 billion compared with last year. This will help us improve facilities for patients. HKL is already 156 years old, so our electrical systems and other infrastructure are different.

“We are already replacing our lifts and upgrading other facilities, and the additional budget will help us upgrade most of the systems as we are planning to go as a full total Health Information System hospital, that means completely computerised,” he told Bernama when met at the Community Programme and Healthy Lifestyle Fun Run held in conjunction with World Heart Day 2026 at Perdana Botanical Gardens here today.
He said HKL was among 16 hospitals scheduled to implement the Health Information System next year, with RM200 million allocated for the initiative.

He said the system would enable specialists from different disciplines to access patients’ medical information electronically, streamlining hospital operations, and reducing the need for patients to repeatedly provide the same information during consultations.

“This will make things easier and improve staff management. Patients will also benefit because they will not have to answer the same questions at every stage of their treatment, as their information will be accessible to specialists across different disciplines,” he said.

On efforts to address non-communicable diseases (NCDs), Dr Harikrishna said the funding was crucial as it would also enable HKL to procure newer medicines and carry out more medical procedures, thereby improving access to treatment.

“With sufficient funding, we can procure more of these medicines and carry out more procedures. We also outsource some simpler cases under Skim Perubatan MADANI, managed by ProtectHealth, and the allocation for this has also been increased,” he said.
Increased funding for outsourcing services would help reduce waiting times, enabling patients to receive treatment sooner and lower the risk of complications.

“Expanding outsourcing services will help reduce waiting times, lower the risk of complications and improve patients’ access to medicines and other treatments. This will be beneficial not only for HKL but also for the Ministry of Health (MOH) as a whole,” he also said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, announced RM47.7 billion for the MOH when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday, up from RM46.5 billion last year.

He also announced RM1.2 billion for the maintenance and repair of public hospitals and clinics, including upgrading the remaining dilapidated clinics, while the allocation for outsourcing patients to other hospitals was increased to RM200 million, alongside expanded collaboration enabling the public healthcare sector to use private healthcare facilities. — Bernama

82ebf0eb7ebbfeb1: OCTOBER 10 — AI can make English easier, but are we truly becoming better English users — or simply better at using AI?

It is hard to ignore the growing presence of artificial intelligence in our daily lives, especially in education. From ChatGPT to grammar checkers and AI writing tools, technology has made learning English more accessible, convenient and, for many students, less intimidating. With just a few prompts, students can receive explanations, vocabulary suggestions, practice questions and even polished essays. It can feel like having a personal tutor available 24/7.

For Malaysian students, particularly those in universities, AI has certainly helped bridge gaps. It can boost confidence, sharpen grammar, expand vocabulary and provide instant feedback. For some learners, it has opened the door to better writing and speaking skills, particularly for those who are shy or lack access to face-to-face support. In many ways, AI has made English learning easier, faster and more efficient.
But here is the real question: has it made us better English users? Or are we simply getting better at using AI?

The concern is not that students are using AI — it is that some are relying on it too much. When AI writes our assignments, corrects our grammar, finds the “right” words and even formulates our ideas, we may be skipping the very process that builds real language proficiency: thinking, struggling and learning from our mistakes.

English is more than just correct grammar and a wide vocabulary. It is a tool for communication, critical thinking and self-expression. When students let AI do all the thinking, they may end up with text that is linguistically correct but lacks originality, personal voice and depth. A perfectly written paragraph means little if the writer has not truly understood the idea behind it.

In speaking, the situation is similar. Many students use AI to practise conversations or generate model answers, but real fluency comes from real interaction — from talking to people, listening to different accents, navigating misunderstandings and learning to express thoughts spontaneously. AI can simulate a conversation, but it cannot completely replace the human element: empathy, cultural nuances and genuine feedback.
AI can make English easier, but are we truly becoming better English users — or simply better at using AI? — Pexels pic

Moreover, there is a risk of becoming too dependent on AI. If students are not careful, they may lose the confidence to write, speak and problem-solve independently. They might also miss out on the valuable experience of struggling a little, making mistakes and growing from them — because that is where real learning happens.

As educators, we too must adapt. The role of the lecturer is no longer simply to teach grammar or vocabulary, but to guide students in using AI wisely. We need to help them develop digital literacy, critical thinking and ethical awareness. AI should be a tool, not a crutch.

And it is important to remember that AI is not always accurate. It can sometimes give incomplete, biased or even incorrect information. Students must learn to question, verify and think critically — skills that are essential not just for language learning, but for life in the digital age.

So, where does this leave us? AI has certainly made English learning easier, and it will continue to be a powerful ally. But true fluency is not just about getting the right answers. It is about developing the ability to use language with confidence, creativity and purpose. That comes from practice, interaction and a genuine interest in the language — not just from a chatbot.

In the end, the goal should not be to become fluent by AI, but to become fluent by habit — through consistent effort, real communication and a willingness to keep learning, with or without technology.
AI can guide us, but it is our curiosity, critical thinking and human connection that will truly make us fluent.
* The author is an English language lecturer at the Centre of Foundation Studies, Universiti Malaya (PASUM), and can be reached at suarnamaran@um.edu.my

14be5be67c2b26a9: PETALING JAYA: Umno Negeri Sembilan sedang mempertimbangkan usul tidak percaya terhadap Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim pada sidang DUN akan datang, menurut sumber.
Sumber yang enggan dinamakan itu mendakwa usul itu akan dikemukakan oleh Ketua Umno Negeri Sembilan Jalaluddin Alias, yang juga Adun Pertang.
"Keputusan kini terletak pada kepimpinan pusat Umno," katanya kepada FMT.
Beliau menambah, barisan baharu Majlis Mesyuarat Kerajaan Negeri (exco) juga mungkin diumumkan sekiranya langkah itu diteruskan.
FMT sedang cuba mendapatkan komen daripada Jalaluddin berhubung perkara ini.
Sidang DUN dijadualkan berlangsung pada 26 Nov selepas ditangguhkan daripada 16 Okt bagi menyelaraskannya dengan pembentangan belanjawan negeri bagi 2027 pada hari berikutnya.

Speaker DUN Awaludin Said sebelum ini memaklumkan, pihaknya belum menerima sebarang notis rasmi mengenai usul tidak percaya terhadap Ismail, menegaskan beliau tidak akan membenarkan usul tergempar sekali pun untuk menjatuhkan menteri besar.

Ismail mengangkat sumpah jawatan sebagai menteri besar pada 2 Ogos susulan PRN yang menyaksikan Barisan Nasional meraih 18 kerusi, Pakatan Harapan 11, manakala Perikatan Nasional memenangi tujuh kerusi.
Pentadbiran beliau bagaimanapun dibayangi krisis perlembagaan berhubung cubaan melucutkan takhta Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar.

Beliau dilaporkan menandatangani proklamasi bagi melucutkan kedudukan baginda pada 3 Ogos. Beliau bagaimanapun mendakwa dipaksa menandatangani dokumen itu dan membuat laporan polis sejurus perkara itu didedahkan kepada umum pada 8 Sept.

Pada 15 Sept, barisan exco Negeri Sembilan mengeluarkan kenyataan mendakwa pelucutan takhta Tuanku Muhriz pada April adalah sah, sekali gus menjadikan Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar pemerintah negeri yang baharu.
Ismail kemudiannya menyokong kenyataan exco itu dan mengarahkan setiausaha kerajaan negeri meneruskan proses pewartaan proklamasi terbabit.

Tuanku Muhriz sejak itu telah membatalkan pelantikan kesemua 10 exco berkenaan, kecuali Ismail. Susulan itu, 10 bekas exco berkenaan memfailkan cabaran undang-undang di mahkamah awal minggu ini bagi menuntut pembatalan pelantikan mereka diisytiharkan tidak sah.
21261505d2069b60: PETALING JAYA: Negeri Sembilan Umno is considering a motion of no confidence against menteri besar Ismail Lasim in the upcoming state assembly meeting, according to a source.
The source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said state Umno chief Jalaluddin Alias, the Pertang assemblyman, would table the motion.
"The decision now rests with the central Umno leadership," the source told FMT.
The source said a new state executive council line-up could also be announced if the move went ahead.
FMT has reached out to Jalaluddin for comment.
The state assembly is scheduled to sit again on Nov 26, having been postponed from Oct 16 to coincide with the tabling of the state’s 2027 budget the following day.

State assembly speaker Awaludin Said had previously said he had not received any formal notice of a no-confidence motion against Ismail, adding that he would not allow even an emergency motion to remove the menteri besar.
Ismail was sworn in as menteri besar on Aug 2 following the state election, in which Barisan Nasional won 18 seats, Pakatan Harapan 11 and Perikatan Nasional seven.
His tenure has since been marred by a constitutional crisis over attempts to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
He reportedly signed a proclamation seeking to remove Tuanku Muhriz on Aug 3. After it was made public on Sept 8, Ismail said he signed the document under duress and lodged a police report.
The Negeri Sembilan exco members on Sept 15 issued a statement claiming that Tuanku Muhriz’s removal in April was legitimate, and that Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar was, therefore, the new ruler.
Ismail subsequently endorsed the exco's statement and ordered the state secretary to proceed with gazetting the proclamation.

Tuanku Muhriz has since revoked the appointments of the 10 excos except Ismail. In turn, earlier this week, the 10 former exco members filed a legal challenge in court seeking to declare the revocation invalid.

f4dab71b611a80df: SINGAPORE, Oct 10 — A total of seven drivers were on Thursday caught for providing illegal cross-border taxi services at Singapore’s land checkpoints.

44ba4420bf94f1e6: NEW DELHI, Oct 10 — India deployed thousands of police in its capital and restricted transportation in and around Delhi ahead of mass demonstrations today demanding the resignation of the country’s election chief over alleged voter-roll irregularities.

The protests, called by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), are the culmination of weeks of opposition mobilisation following allegations of misconduct during a nationwide voter-roll revision.
Demonstrations erupted across the country after a newspaper investigation last month alleged misconduct by the Election Commission of India (ECI).
The ECI has rejected allegations of impropriety in the “special intensive revision”, saying it was intended to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.
Opposition parties and critics say the exercise could disenfranchise voters to the benefit of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Tens of thousands of police officers and paramilitary personnel have been deployed across the capital, with multiple layers of yellow metal barricades blocking roads leading to Jantar Mantar, the usual government-designated protest site.
Police have not authorised rallies at the site this weekend.
The protests, called by the CJP, are widely seen as a reprise of its mass mobilisation in July, which led to the education minister stepping down over an examination scandal.
This time, they are demanding ECI chief Gyanesh Kumar resign.

Pedestrians walk away after police personnel barricaded a street ahead of a protest by the youth-led Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) demanding the resignation of India’s Chief Election Commissioner over alleged ‘special intensive revision’ (SIR) voter-roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi October 10, 2026. — AFP pic
‘Cannot detain the movement’
The allegations are a fresh challenge for 76-year-old Modi during his third term in office.
Authorities have ordered the closure of dozens of metro stations, and cancelled several trains coming to New Delhi.
However, the Supreme Court yesterday said some trains must still run and that there should be no blanket closure of metro stations.

“The dictator would rather shut down the entire national capital and inconvenience millions of citizens than allow a peaceful protest at a designated protest site,” CJP chief Abhijeet Dipke said on X.
“Imagine how many lives would be affected because of this shutdown by Modi.”
The CJP, which emerged online as a satirical political movement in May, has accused authorities of intimidating its supporters ahead of the demonstration.
The party has said that “at least 10,000 people”, including protesters travelling to Delhi by train, have been detained across the country.

The deal comes weeks before key US elections where Trump’s Republican Party risks losing its grip on Congress as voters express frustration over the mounting cost of living.

Zelensky told reporters: “It is certainly not honest, it is certainly unworthy of our partners, and it is, in my view, a weak decision.”

“Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority,” Trump posted on social media.
Conflict stalemate

The average cost of regular US gasoline has jumped more than 46 per cent since late February to US$4.37 (RM17.85) per gallon, while that of diesel rocketed 67 per cent over the same period to US$6.28 per gallon.

News of the deal came as Ukrainian and US negotiators met yesterday in Miami in a fresh attempt to break the conflict’s stalemate.
The sides “held constructive discussions on potential avenues to de-escalate and conclude the war with Russia ahead of winter,” said US envoy Steve Witkoff.

The Miami meeting follows visits to Moscow and Kyiv last month by Witkoff, a longtime Trump confidant, and Jared Kushner, the president’s son-in-law, as Washington seeks to revive negotiations that have yielded little progress.
With winter approaching, the prospect of continued fighting and attacks on vital infrastructure has added urgency to the search for a settlement against a backdrop of deadly Russian attacks.
On Thursday, a Russian strike on buses in the frontline Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk killed 30 people.

Trump’s repeated attempts to broker an end to the war have foundered over Moscow’s sweeping territorial demands, particularly its insistence on controlling all of Ukraine’s eastern Donbas region, including areas still held by Kyiv.
Zelensky has rejected surrendering Ukrainian-held territory, warning that Russia could use it as a springboard for another attack.
Russia now occupies roughly one-fifth of Ukrainian territory.

The Miami discussions covered “security guarantees, as well as longer-term arrangements for Ukraine’s and Europe’s security to prevent future conflicts, and support Ukraine’s post-war reconstruction,” Witkoff said.
Officials from Britain, France and Germany were at the talks, along with representatives of Nato and the European Union. — AFP

4d7b65ea1709ea27: From Helmy Haja Mydin

Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim rarely presents a budget without a literary flourish. Tabling his latest on Oct 9, Anwar cited Isaiah Berlin, John Rawls and Homer, among others. He also offered a slogan: "reach for the sky, stay rooted in the earth".
As with all budgets, the numbers need to match the words. Thankfully, they do in this one.
The statistics

Malaysia’s GDP grew by 6% year-on-year in the second quarter. Among Southeast Asia’s six biggest economies, only Vietnam, at 8.4%, did better. Singapore managed 5.9% and Indonesia 5.3%, while Thailand and the Philippines grew by about 2%.

Inflation is around 2%, while the ringgit has held roughly steady against the US dollar this year. In June, Swiss business school IMD ranked Malaysia the world’s 15th most competitive economy, second in the region to Singapore.

Some of this stability comes at a cost. Fuel subsidies will cost about RM40 billion this year after the war in West Asia lifted oil prices, pushing the fiscal deficit to 3.6% of GDP. Federal debt is around 64% of GDP.
Much of the boom also depends on global demand for AI hardware, which Malaysia’s chip-packagers and data centres supply. The Asian Development Bank expects growth to ease to 4.7% next year.
Budget targets

The budget’s showpiece measures are aimed at households. Total outlays, including investment by state-linked funds, increased to RM510 billion. Operating spending climbed by 11%, while development spending is up by just 2.5%.

Cash and grocery aid, which totalled RM8 billion in 2022, will reach RM16 billion next year. Adults outside the main cash-aid scheme will receive RM100 in grocery credit twice in 2027. Doctors who finish their training in government hospitals are promised permanent jobs, ending years of short contracts.

Personal tax relief has been increased for the first time since 2010, and the minimum wage goes from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month effective June 2027. Small and medium-sized firms with sales under RM50 million are exempt, to give them time to adjust. Such firms employ about half the workforce.

By regional standards, this is a sensible mix. Indonesia promises to cut its deficit to 2.4% of GDP next year while paying for President Prabowo Subianto’s free-meals programme; Standard Chartered, a bank, forecast 2.9% in August.
Filipinos are watching 7% inflation eat their wages. Malaysia replaced blanket fuel subsidies with targeted ones, recycled the savings into household aid, and has made the change stick.
Room for development
The weak spot is productivity and the pay that should follow it. Employee compensation is just 33.9% of GDP, against a government target of 40% by 2030.

The data-centre boom has been capital-heavy and job-light: 143 projects approved between 2021 and mid-2025, worth RM144 billion, promised 1,429 jobs, roughly RM100 million per job. Three changes might help.

Medical devices offer one. Malaysia exported RM34.5 billion of them last year, but much of the high-end output comes from multinationals, such as Boston Scientific and Dexcom, whose products are designed abroad.
The health ministry could help by weighing clinical outcomes and lifetime cost alongside price, and by trialling promising local designs, giving their makers a first reference customer.

MediAsas, a new insurance plan that pays hospitals by diagnosis, should push private hospitals the same way. The Medical Device Authority (MDA) now works more efficiently and with multiple neighbouring regulators, sparing firms duplicate reviews. Asean-wide reliance, running in both directions, would make a Malaysian approval a passport to nearly 700 million people.
Digital policy is the second change. Electricity and water are now tight enough that the government has been turning away data centres that do not serve AI.
Remaining grid capacity should go to projects that bring workloads, research and skilled jobs, and the incentives attached to MDEC’s Malaysia Digital status could be tied to those outcomes.
MDEC’s RM30 million fund, announced in the budget, will help 4,000 small firms adopt AI and train 5,000 AI professionals, under RM3,500 per firm or trainee. That is a pilot; it deserves scale.

The two strands meet in health. The communications regulator is putting RM1 billion into electronic medical records, and the device regulator already runs an AI sandbox. Together they could make Malaysia Asean’s testbed for clinical AI, provided patients’ data are guarded.
Experiential travel

Live events are the third lever. A local promoter estimated that Malaysia hosted more than 400 concerts in 2024, generating over RM553 million in tourism and related spending, and that the industry could contribute nearly RM1.7 billion this year.

Demand is strong. The indoor Unifi Arena at Bukit Jalil is booked every weekend. When Formula One returned to Sepang this month, Hong Leong Bank reckoned it would add RM1.1 billion to RM1.3 billion of output, with the average visitor spending nearly RM9,000.
Malaysia hosts the SEA Games in September 2027, and the venue upgrades due to finish by March should leave them fit for promoters, broadcasters and hospitality buyers as well as athletes.

The budget offers a rebate for organisers at venues seating 10,000 or more, but waives entertainment duty for concerts and sport only at Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara. Extending the waiver to all large venues would help Kuala Lumpur compete with Singapore as Southeast Asia’s entertainment hub.

Anwar’s closing passage invoked Odysseus, who took 10 years to return to Ithaca. Malaysia set out for developed-country status in 1991, with 2020 as its arrival date. Its economy is better equipped for the rest of the voyage than most of its neighbours’. How fast it gets there depends on what each worker produces.

Helmy Haja Mydin chairs the Social & Economic Research Initiative (SERI) and Perbadanan Stadium Malaysia, sits on the boards of MDEC and the MDA and practises as a consultant physician in a private hospital.

23c6daf64509b395: When news of the Aug 26 Nepal glacial and flood disaster broke, Dr Manivannan Rethinam’s first thoughts went out to his sister Komathi who was on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash.
Together with her husband, he tried but failed to reach her. She is among 54 Malaysians still listed as missing. No one knows if they are still alive, and that is the problem.
Since then, Manivannan, who heads the Malaysian Solidarity Families in Hope support group dealing with the authorities, has learned a brutal truth: there is no sympathy in bureaucracy or the law.
Without a death certificate, spouses and children have no access to joint bank accounts or the victim’s EPF savings. They cannot sell family homes nor cancel hire purchase contracts.
All the banks can do is express sympathy for their loss. Without a death certificate, they cannot act, and without a body identified through DNA, a death certificate cannot be issued.
The DNA dilemma
And herein lies the cruellest of ironies: the bodies may never be found.
Nepalese rescue teams have spent weeks searching, but the terrain is treacherous and inaccessible. Officials have privately admitted that finding all 54 bodies is “unlikely”.

Insurance companies, meanwhile, cannot pay out on life policies. Their position is legally defensible: without a death certificate, there is no confirmation of death. DNA identification requires a body. No body means no DNA. No DNA, no death certificate. No death certificate, no payout.
This Catch-22 situation is driving the affected families to despair.

Compounding the agony is the legal inconsistency between Malaysia and Nepal. Under Malaysian law, a person can legally be declared dead only after being missing for seven years. In Nepal, it takes only three years.
The question is which jurisdiction takes precedence. The answer, according to Malaysian legal experts, is murky.
Those missing are Malaysian citizens, so Malaysian law governs their estates. But the deaths occurred on Nepalese soil. The question of jurisdiction may take years to resolve in courts.
According to Manivannan the Malaysian embassy in Kathmandu has agreed to accept Nepal’s jurisdiction over this, but that is only a verbal assurance.
For one person, the pain has taken a particularly bitter form.
His wife had bought a new car just months before she left for Nepal. Now the husband faces an impossible choice.
He cannot afford the monthly instalments on his own, along with the mortgage and his children’s expenses. He decided to return the car to the bank, surrendering it to stop the bleeding.
But the bank’s response was clinical. They asked him to stop payments for three months, and they will repossess the vehicle.
But that raises another problem — he will be liable for the default penalty, the repossession charges, and any shortfall between the auction price and the outstanding loan balance.
Information blackout
Perhaps most agonising of all is the silence.

The missing person’s next-of-kin cannot obtain any information about their loved one’s financial accounts. Bank Negara has strict confidentiality laws that prevent banks from disclosing account details to family members without a power of attorney or a court order.
But how do you get a power of attorney from a person who is missing?

Manivannan says the families are unable to get the August salary of their breadwinners who are missing because employers can only deposit the money in the missing person’s bank account. “Employers cannot release it to the next-of-kin,” he pointed out.
For some families, the tragedy is almost too vast to comprehend.

The credit cards of those missing are still active, and utility bills must still be paid. Worse than that insurance companies may kickstart automatic premium loan to keep policies alive although the insured may eventually be declared dead.
It is a technicality that the Life Insurance Association of Malaysia and Bank Negara must quickly resolve to prevent more financial losses.
Calls for Bank Negara to step in
Families and advocates now want Bank Negara to intervene.

“We need Bank Negara to issue a directive to all financial institutions: freeze all payments, waive all penalties, suspend all repossessions, and allow next-of-kin access to accounts based on a police report of the disappearance — not a death certificate,” says Manivannan.
More needs to be done. The government must consider emergency legislative measures to address the seven-year rule in exceptional disaster situations.

There must also be mechanisms for insurance companies and financial institutions to provide appropriate interim assistance to affected families while the legal status of their loved ones remains unresolved.

Behind every legal argument, every bureaucratic hurdle, every frozen account, there is a human being — a wife who cannot sleep, a child who cannot concentrate at school, a parent who cannot stop crying.

5724ecb12ef259ab: From Moaz Nair
The government’s phased initiative to dismantle the contract system for medical officers by 2028 under civil service reforms is a commendable stride forward.

The health ministry's Inter-Ministerial Joint Task Force (IMJTF) targets that, by 2028, every single graduate medical officer (houseman) who completes training will be offered a permanent role immediately.
Alongside plans to absorb remaining contract doctors in waves throughout 2027, this milestone stands to dissolve years of systemic gridlock.

Various measures have also been introduced to encourage more young medical officers to serve in Sabah and Sarawak. These initiatives include improving the placement system, fully covering relocation expenses, and granting additional merit points for specialist training and study leave applications to those deployed in the two regions.

However, if the ministry truly wants to eradicate career uncertainty for young doctors, it must maintain momentum through absolute policy transparency. Permanent job security means little if the job itself remains structurally unsustainable.
The underlying crisis

Securing a permanent position is no longer the ultimate retention tool it once was. The ministry faces an ongoing talent drain, as permanent medical officers continue to resign due to acute workforce pressures.

Chief among these triggers is the operational environment. Extreme workloads and severe burnout—compounded by gruelling on-call hours and systemic understaffing at key facilities—are directly eroding the mental and physical well-being of frontline officers. A toxic workplace culture, notably the persistence of bullying, further compromises their emotional health.

This structural stress is intensified by friction within the e-Placement system. Abrupt, ill-prepared regional transfers, combined with historical inequities in relocation allowances, have frequently left physicians feeling trapped, viewing resignation as the only reasonable exit strategy.

When coupled with personal sacrifices—whether managing family logistics, navigating chronic health challenges, or funding independent specialist pathways—the public healthcare system becomes increasingly difficult to justify for young talent.
Strategic roadmap for systemic retention
To preserve the integrity of our national health service, the state must match its hiring pledges with deep, structural interventions:

Restructuring financial rewards: the government must bridge the income gap between the public and private sectors through periodic reviews of salaries and allowances. This measure includes reassessing the critical service allowance, increasing on-call allowance rates, and introducing specialised incentive models for senior clinical specialists. Furthermore, extending fair locum payment rates is essential to ensure that every hour of overtime is met with commensurate financial compensation.

Reforming workplace culture: the ministry must shift from rhetoric to strict enforcement regarding its zero-tolerance policy against hospital bullying. Introducing humane, flexible scheduling is a prerequisite to mitigating chronic burnout.

Transparent e-Placement logistics: the e-Placement mechanism must operate with predictability, affording doctors reasonable notice windows to arrange their personal lives. Incorporating voluntary placement options or regional preferences would heavily boost morale. Crucially, full relocation allowances must be distributed equitably across all tenures to curb the financial shocks of interstate transfers.

Securing specialisation pathways: access to advanced postgraduate tracks, whether via the federal training award (HLP) or parallel pathways, must be expanded and streamlined. Young physicians need to see an unambiguous, rewarding long-term trajectory within the public civil service.
The bottom line

Retaining our public medical workforce goes far beyond baseline worker welfare; it is a critical investment in the sovereignty and resilience of Malaysia’s healthcare framework. The resignation trends tell a clear story: toxic environments and career instability are the primary drivers of our talent flight.

By balancing the 2028 permanent employment pledge with meaningful, systemic workplace and financial updates, the ministry can successfully turn the tide. Safeguarding a competent and motivated healthcare workforce is the only definitive way to ensure every Malaysian retains access to equitable, high-quality and affordable care.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.
